title.zh: 卷262 列傳四十九 魏裔介 熊赐履 李光地
title.en: Volume 262 Biographies 49: Wei Yijie, Xiong Cilv, Li Guangdi
title.raw: 卷262 列傳四十九 魏裔介 熊赐履 李光地

sentences.zh: 魏裔介，字石生，直隸柏鄉人。

translations.literal: Wei Yijie, styled Shisheng, was a man of Baixiang in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yijie, whose style was Shisheng, came from Baixiang in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 順治三年進士，選庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shunzhi he became a jinshi and was selected as a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 3 (1646) he passed the jinshi examination and was chosen as a Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 四年，授工科給事中。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed supervising secretary of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made supervising secretary of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 五年，疏請舉經筵及時講學，以隆治本。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he memorialized requesting that the Classics Lecture be held and study pursued in timely fashion, to elevate fundamental governance.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he submitted a memorial asking that the emperor hold regular Classics Lectures and study without delay, so as to strengthen the foundations of rule.

sentences.zh: 又言：「燕、趙之民，椎牛裹糧，首先歸命。

translations.literal: He also said: "The people of Yan and Zhao slaughtered cattle and wrapped grain, being the first to submit.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "The people of Yan and Zhao slaughtered cattle and packed provisions to be the first to submit to the new dynasty.

sentences.zh: 此漢高之關中，光武之河內也。

translations.literal: This is like Gaozu of Han's Guanzhong and Guangwu's Henei.
translations.idiomatic: They were to the Qing what Guanzhong had been to Gaozu of Han and Henei to Emperor Guangwu.

sentences.zh: 今天下初定，屢奉詔蠲賦，而畿輔未霑實惠，宜切責奉行之吏，彰信於民。」

translations.literal: Now that the realm is newly settled, decrees for tax remission have been issued repeatedly, yet the capital region has not received the real benefit; the officials charged with implementation should be sternly held accountable, so that trust is made clear to the people."
translations.idiomatic: Now that the realm is newly pacified, repeated edicts have remitted taxes, yet the capital districts have not felt the real benefit. Officials charged with carrying out these orders should be held strictly accountable so that the government's word is made credible to the people.

sentences.zh: 俱報聞。

translations.literal: All were acknowledged.
translations.idiomatic: All of these proposals were noted by the throne.

sentences.zh: 轉吏科，以母憂歸。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Secretariat Section and returned home on account of his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to the Secretariat Section, he went home to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，九年，起故官。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, in the ninth year he was restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning period ended, in the ninth year he was recalled to his former post.

sentences.zh: 應詔疏言：「上下之情未通，滿、漢之氣中閼。

translations.literal: Responding to an imperial edict he submitted a memorial saying: "Sentiment above and below is not connected; Manchu and Han atmosphere is blocked in the middle.
translations.idiomatic: In response to an imperial call for candid memorials, he wrote: "Feeling between ruler and subjects has not yet opened; the spirit between Manchu and Han remains obstructed in the middle.

sentences.zh: 大臣闒茸以保富貴，小臣鉗結以習功名。

translations.literal: Great ministers are negligent to preserve wealth and rank; petty officials are constricted to acquire fame and merit.
translations.idiomatic: Senior ministers grow slack to protect their wealth and status, while junior officials hold their tongues to secure promotion and reputation.

sentences.zh: 紀綱日弛，法度日壞。

translations.literal: Discipline daily slackens; laws and regulations daily decay.
translations.idiomatic: Discipline grows lax by the day, and statutes and precedents erode daily.

sentences.zh: 請時禦正殿，召對群臣，虛心諮訪。

translations.literal: I request that Your Majesty regularly enter the main hall, summon and face the ministers, and consult with an open mind.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to hold court regularly in the main hall, summon the ministers for direct audience, and seek their counsel with an open mind.

sentences.zh: 令部院科道等官面奏政事，仍令史官記註，以求救時之實。」

translations.literal: Order officials of the ministries, courts, censorate sections and circuits to report on state affairs in person, and still have historiographers record and annotate, to seek the reality of saving the times."
translations.idiomatic: Let ministers, department heads, and censorate officials present affairs in person, with historiographers still taking note, so that the court may learn what is truly needed to rescue the age.

sentences.zh: 時世祖親政，裔介疏言：「督撫重臣宜慎選擇，不宜專用遼左舊人。」

translations.literal: At this time the Shizu Emperor personally took power; Yijie submitted a memorial saying: "Governors-general and governors are weighty ministers and should be chosen with care; one should not employ only old men from Liaodong exclusively."
translations.idiomatic: By then the Shizu Emperor had begun to rule in person. Yijie memorialized: "Provincial governors and governors-general are posts of the greatest weight and should be chosen with care; the court ought not rely exclusively on veterans from the old Liaodong circle.

sentences.zh: 又言：「攝政王時，隱匿逃人，立法太嚴，天下囂然，喪其樂生之心。

translations.literal: He also said: "Under the Prince Regent, concealing fugitive laborers—the law was too severe; the realm was in uproar and lost the heart to rejoice in life.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Under the Prince Regent, laws against harboring fugitive bondsmen were so harsh that the whole country seethed and people lost the will to make a living.

sentences.zh: 後以言官陳說，始寬其禁，責成州縣，法至善也。

translations.literal: Later, because censorial officials stated the case, the prohibition was first relaxed and responsibility was placed on prefectures and counties—the law was most excellent.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after remonstrating officials explained the harm, the prohibition was eased and enforcement was entrusted to prefectures and counties—a policy that was altogether sound.

sentences.zh: 若捨此之外別有峻法，竊恐下拂人心，上乾天和，非尋常政治小小得失而已。」

translations.literal: If apart from this there are other severe laws, I fear privately that below people's hearts will be alienated and above Heaven's harmony will be disturbed—this is not a small gain or loss of ordinary politics."
translations.idiomatic: If, abandoning this approach, the court adopts still harsher measures, I fear it will alienate the people below and offend Heaven's harmony above—far more than the usual petty gains and losses of routine administration.

sentences.zh: 上韙之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor endorsed his views.

sentences.zh: 河南巡撫吳景道援恩詔薦舉明兵部尚書張縉彥。

translations.literal: Henan Governor Wu Jingdao, citing the amnesty edict, recommended the former Ming Minister of War Zhang Jinyan.
translations.idiomatic: Henan Governor Wu Jingdao, invoking the general amnesty edict, recommended Zhang Jinyan, former Minister of War under the Ming.

sentences.zh: 裔介疏言：「縉彥仕明，身任中樞，養寇誤國，有盧杞、賈似道之姦，而庸劣過之。

translations.literal: Yijie submitted a memorial saying: "Jinyan served the Ming, personally held the central pivot, nourished bandits and harmed the state, had the treachery of Lu Qi and Jia Sidao, yet surpassed them in mediocrity and inferiority.
translations.idiomatic: Yijie memorialized: "Jinyan served the Ming at the center of power, indulged rebels, and ruined the state. He had the treachery of a Lu Qi or Jia Sidao, yet was even more mediocre and incompetent than they.

sentences.zh: 宜予擯棄，以協公論。」

translations.literal: He should be rejected, to accord with public opinion."
translations.idiomatic: He ought to be rejected outright, in keeping with public opinion.

sentences.zh: 疏下部議，以事在赦前，予外用。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down to the ministries for deliberation; because the matter was before the amnesty, he was given external appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the ministries, which ruled that because the offense predated the amnesty, Jinyan might be given an appointment outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「州縣遇災荒，既經報部，其例得蠲緩錢糧，即予停徵，以杜吏胥欺隱。

translations.literal: He again submitted a memorial saying: "When prefectures and counties encounter famine, once reported to the ministry, grain and money that by precedent may be remitted or deferred should immediately have collection suspended, to stop clerks and runners from concealment and fraud.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed that when a prefecture or county reported a disaster to the ministry, any taxes eligible for remission or deferral under precedent should at once cease to be collected, so that clerks could not continue to extort the people in secret.

sentences.zh: 並就州縣積穀及存貯庫銀，先行賑貸。」

translations.literal: Moreover, from prefectural and county granary reserves and stored treasury silver, relief loans should first be advanced."
translations.idiomatic: Local granary stocks and treasury reserves on hand should be used at once for relief loans.

sentences.zh: 下所司議行。

translations.literal: It was sent down to the responsible offices for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was referred to the relevant offices and put into effect.

sentences.zh: 時直隸、河南、山東諸省災，別疏請賑。

translations.literal: At this time Zhili, Henan, Shandong and other provinces suffered disaster; he separately memorialized requesting relief.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhili, Henan, Shandong, and other provinces were stricken by famine, he submitted a separate memorial requesting relief.

sentences.zh: 上命發帑金二十四萬，分遣大臣賑之，全活甚眾。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered 240,000 taels from the treasury to be issued and grand ministers dispatched to relieve them; very many were wholly saved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered 240,000 taels from the treasury and dispatched senior ministers to administer relief, saving a great multitude of lives.

sentences.zh: 十一年，遷兵科都給事中。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was transferred to chief supervising secretary of the Military Section.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was promoted to chief supervising secretary of the Military Section.

sentences.zh: 東南兵事未定，疏言：「今日劉文秀復起於川南，孫可望竊據於貴築，李定國伺隙於西粵，張名振流氛於海島，連年征討，尚稽天誅。

translations.literal: Southeastern military affairs were not settled; he submitted a memorial saying: "Today Liu Wenxiu has risen again in southern Sichuan, Sun Kewang illicitly holds Guiyang, Li Dingguo watches for openings in western Guangdong, Zhang Mingzhen's wandering miasma is on the sea islands—year after year we campaign, yet Heaven's punishment still delays.
translations.idiomatic: With fighting in the southeast still unresolved, he wrote: "Liu Wenxiu has risen again in southern Sichuan, Sun Kewang holds Guiyang, Li Dingguo waits for an opening in western Guangdong, and Zhang Mingzhen roams the coastal islands. Campaigns drag on year after year, yet Heaven's judgment on these rebels still tarries.

sentences.zh: 為目前進取計，蜀為滇、黔門戶，蜀既守而滇、黔之勢蹙，故蜀不可不先取。

translations.literal: For the present plan of advance, Shu is the gateway to Yunnan and Guizhou; once Shu is held the momentum of Yunnan and Guizhou is cramped—therefore Shu cannot but be taken first.
translations.idiomatic: For the immediate campaign, Sichuan is the gateway to Yunnan and Guizhou: once Sichuan is secured, the enemy in Yunnan and Guizhou is cramped, so Sichuan must be taken first.

sentences.zh: 此西南之情形也。

translations.literal: This is the situation in the southwest.
translations.idiomatic: Such is the situation in the southwest.

sentences.zh: 粵西稍弱，昨歲桂林之役未大創，必圖再犯，以牽制我湖南之師。

translations.literal: Guangxi is somewhat weaker; last year's battle at Guilin did not inflict a great wound—they will surely plan to invade again to pin down our Hunan army.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi is somewhat weaker: last year's battle at Guilin did not cripple the rebels, and they will surely try again to tie down our forces in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 宜令籓鎮更番迭出，相機戰守。

translations.literal: The feudatory commands should be ordered to rotate in and out in succession and fight or hold as circumstances allow.
translations.idiomatic: The regional commands should rotate troops in turn and seize opportunities to attack or defend as conditions require.

sentences.zh: 此三方者，攻瑕宜先粵西。

translations.literal: Among these three directions, in attacking weak points Guangxi should come first.
translations.idiomatic: Of these three fronts, the weakest point—and the one to strike first—is Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 粵西潰則可望膽落，滇、黔亦當瓦解。」

translations.literal: If Guangxi collapses then Kewang's courage will fall, and Yunnan and Guizhou also ought to disintegrate."
translations.idiomatic: Once Guangxi collapses, Kewang will lose heart, and Yunnan and Guizhou should follow in dissolution.

sentences.zh: 又疏劾湖南將軍續順公沈永忠擁兵觀望，致總兵官徐勇、辰常道劉昇祚力竭戰死。

translations.literal: He also submitted a memorial impeaching Hunan General Xushun Gong Shen Yongzhong for holding troops and watching from the sidelines, causing Regional Commander Xu Yong and Chenchang Circuit Intendant Liu Shengzuo to fight to exhaustion and die in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached Hunan General Shen Yongzhong, Prince Xushun, for holding his army back while watching events unfold, with the result that Regional Commander Xu Yong and Chenchang Circuit Intendant Liu Shengzuo fought until spent and died on the field.

sentences.zh: 永忠坐罷任奪爵。

translations.literal: Yongzhong was punished by dismissal from office and deprivation of rank.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhong was dismissed from his post and stripped of his title.

sentences.zh: 复劾福建提督楊名高玩寇，致漳州郡縣為鄭成功淪陷，名高坐罷任。

translations.literal: He again impeached Fujian Provincial Commander Yang Minggao for indulging the bandits, causing Zhangzhou prefecture and counties to fall to Zheng Chenggong; Minggao was punished by dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached Fujian Provincial Commander Yang Minggao for treating the enemy lightly, which led to the fall of Zhangzhou and its subordinate districts to Zheng Chenggong; Minggao was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 尋遷太常寺少卿，擢左副都御史。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and promoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and then promoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 十三年，疏劾大學士陳之遴營私植黨，之遴坐解官，發遼陽閒住。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he submitted a memorial impeaching Grand Secretary Chen Zhibian for pursuing private interests and planting factions; Zhibian was punished by removal from office and sent to reside at leisure in Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he impeached Grand Secretary Chen Zhibian for faction-building and self-dealing. Zhibian was dismissed and sent to live in retirement at Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 十四年，遷左都御史，上諭之曰：「朕擢用汝，非繇人薦達。」

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to Left Censor-in-Chief; the emperor instructed him, saying: "I have promoted and employed you—not through others' recommendation and advancement."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he became Left Censor-in-Chief. The emperor told him, "I promoted you myself; no one else brought you to my attention.

sentences.zh: 裔介益感奮，盡所欲言。

translations.literal: Yijie was all the more moved and inspired, speaking all he wished to say.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply stirred, Yijie spoke his mind without reserve.

sentences.zh: 四月，因欽天監推算次月日月交食，疏請廣言路，緩工作，寬州縣考成，速頒恩赦，釋滯獄，酌复五品以下官俸，減徵調之兵，節供應之費。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, because the Directorate of Astronomy calculated solar and lunar eclipses for the next month, he memorialized requesting broadening of the avenue of speech, slowing works, relaxing prefectural and county performance assessments, speedy issuance of amnesties, release of long-pending cases, consideration of restoring salaries for officials of the fifth rank and below, reduction of conscripted troops, and economizing on supply expenses.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, when the Directorate of Astronomy forecast eclipses for the coming month, he urged the court to widen free speech, slow major construction, ease performance reviews for local officials, issue an amnesty promptly, clear long-pending cases, restore salaries for officials of the fifth rank and below where possible, cut troop levies, and reduce court expenditures.

sentences.zh: 上嘉之，下部詳議以行。

translations.literal: The emperor praised it and sent it down to the ministries for detailed deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended the memorial and referred it to the ministries for detailed implementation.

sentences.zh: 嘗侍經筵，講漢文帝春和之詔，因舉仁政所宜先者數事。

translations.literal: He once attended the Classics Lecture, expounding Emperor Wen of Han's edict on spring harmony, and thereupon cited several matters that benevolent government should put first.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while attending the Classics Lecture, he discussed Emperor Wen of Han's edict on springtime harmony and went on to list several priorities for humane government.

sentences.zh: 正陽門外菜園為前朝嘉蔬圃地，久為民居，部議入官。

translations.literal: The vegetable gardens outside Zhengyang Gate were the former dynasty's imperial vegetable plots, long since dwellings; the ministry deliberated taking them into government ownership.
translations.idiomatic: The market gardens outside Zhengyang Gate had been imperial vegetable plots in the previous dynasty but had long been occupied as residences; the ministry proposed reclaiming them for the state.

sentences.zh: 裔介過其地，民走訴，即入告，仍以予民。

translations.literal: Yijie passed that place; the people ran to complain; he immediately entered to report, and the land was still given back to the people.
translations.idiomatic: When Yijie passed the area, residents rushed to plead with him. He reported at once to the throne, and the land was returned to them.

sentences.zh: 十六年，加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was given the additional title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十七年，京察自陳。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, at the capital personnel review, he submitted a self-assessment.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he filed a self-assessment at the metropolitan personnel review.

sentences.zh: 以御史巡方屢坐貪敗，責裔介未糾劾，削太子太保，供職如故。

translations.literal: Because touring censors repeatedly were punished for corruption and failure, Yijie was blamed for not having impeached them; his Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent title was stripped, but he continued in office as before.
translations.idiomatic: Because several touring censors had been found guilty of corruption on his watch, he was faulted for failing to impeach them in time. He lost the Grand Guardian title but retained his post.

sentences.zh: 時可望猶據貴州，鄭成功亂未已。

translations.literal: At this time Kewang still held Guizhou and Zheng Chenggong's rebellion had not ended.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Kewang still held Guizhou, and Zheng Chenggong's rebellion on the coast had not yet ended.

sentences.zh: 裔介疏言：「可望恃峒蠻為助，宜命在事諸臣加意招徠，予以新敕印，舊者毋即收繳，則歸我者必多。

translations.literal: Yijie submitted a memorial saying: "Kewang relies on Dong barbarians as aid; the ministers on the scene should be ordered to devote special care to winning men over, grant them new imperial patents and seals, and not immediately collect the old ones—then those who come over to us will surely be many.
translations.idiomatic: Yijie wrote: "Kewang relies on the Dong peoples. Officials in the field should be ordered to win defectors over carefully, grant new patents and seals, and not demand the surrender of old ones at once—then many more will come over to us.

sentences.zh: 成功作亂海上，我水師無多，惟於沿海要地增兵築堡，使不得泊岸劫掠，然後招其攜貳，散其黨與，海患可以漸平。」

translations.literal: Chenggong makes rebellion on the sea; our naval forces are not many—only at key points along the coast should troops be increased and forts built so that they cannot anchor and plunder ashore; then entice their wavering followers and scatter their partisans, and the sea trouble can gradually be pacified."
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong's rebellion at sea cannot be crushed at once, for our fleet is small. We should reinforce key coastal points and build forts so that his ships cannot land to raid; then we may win over waverers and break up his following, and the maritime threat can be reduced step by step.

sentences.zh: 下部議行。

translations.literal: It was sent down to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the ministries and carried out.

sentences.zh: 未幾，疏劾大學士劉正宗、成克鞏欺罔附和諸罪，命正宗、克鞏回奏，未得實，下法司勘訊，並解裔介官與質。

translations.literal: Before long he submitted a memorial impeaching Grand Secretaries Liu Zhengzong and Cheng Ke'gong for deception, collusion and other crimes; the emperor ordered Zhengzong and Ke'gong to reply; facts were not obtained; it was sent down to the judicial offices for investigation, and Yijie's office was also removed for cross-examination.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he impeached Grand Secretaries Liu Zhengzong and Cheng Ke'gong for deceit and factional collusion. Ordered to respond, they could not substantiate their defense, and the case was referred to the judicial offices. Yijie was also temporarily removed from office to testify.

sentences.zh: 讞定，正宗獲罪籍沒，克鞏奪職視事，复裔介官。

translations.literal: When the verdict was fixed, Zhengzong was found guilty and his property confiscated; Ke'gong was deprived of office but continued duties; Yijie's office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When judgment was rendered, Zhengzong was convicted and his property confiscated; Ke'gong was stripped of rank but kept at his duties; Yijie was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 時以雲南、福建用兵，加派錢糧。

translations.literal: At this time because of military campaigns in Yunnan and Fujian, additional levies of grain and money were assigned.
translations.idiomatic: Because of the campaigns in Yunnan and Fujian, extra grain and money levies were imposed.

sentences.zh: 裔介疏請敕戶部綜計軍需足用即停止，上命未派者並停止。

translations.literal: Yijie memorialized requesting an imperial order to the Ministry of Revenue to calculate comprehensively: once military needs were sufficient, levies should stop; the emperor ordered that those not yet assigned should also stop.
translations.idiomatic: Yijie asked the throne to instruct the Ministry of Revenue to tally military needs and halt surcharges as soon as supplies were adequate. The emperor ordered that even levies not yet dispatched should be canceled.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，雲南既定，疏言：「雲南既有吳三桂籓兵數万，及督提兩標兵，則滿洲兵可撤。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi, when Yunnan was already settled, he submitted a memorial saying: "Yunnan already has Wu Sangui's feudatory troops numbering tens of thousands, plus the two standards of the governor-general and provincial commander—then Manchu troops may be withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 1 (1662), after Yunnan had been pacified, he wrote: "With Wu Sangui's feudatory force of tens of thousands in Yunnan, together with the governor-general's and provincial commander's two standards, the Manchu garrison may be withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 但滇、黔、川、楚邊方遼遠，不以滿洲兵鎮守要地，倘戎寇生心，恐鞭長莫及。

translations.literal: But the borderlands of Yunnan, Guizhou, Sichuan and Huguang are remote and far; if Manchu troops do not garrison key places, should barbarian raiders take heart, I fear the whip will not reach.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the frontiers of Yunnan, Guizhou, Sichuan, and Huguang are vast and distant. Without Manchu troops at critical points, if enemies should stir, the court may find its reach too short.

sentences.zh: 荊、襄乃天下腹心，宜擇大將領滿兵數千駐防，無事則控制形勢，可以銷姦宄之萌；

translations.literal: Jing and Xiang are the belly and heart of the realm; a great general should be chosen to lead several thousand Manchu troops to garrison them—when there is no affair they control the strategic situation and can extinguish the sprouting of treachery and villainy;
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou and Xiangyang are the strategic center of the empire. A senior commander should be chosen to station several thousand Manchu troops there. In peace they would control the terrain and nip conspiracy in the bud;

sentences.zh: 有事則提兵應援，可以據水陸之勝。」

translations.literal: when there is an affair they can raise troops to respond in aid and hold the advantage of water and land."
translations.idiomatic: in war they could march to reinforce other fronts and hold the advantage of both river and road.

sentences.zh: 疏下部，格不行。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down to the ministries but blocked and not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred downward but blocked and not adopted.

sentences.zh: 復請以湖廣總督移駐荊州，從之。

translations.literal: He again requested that the Huguang Governor-General be moved to garrison at Jingzhou; this was followed.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that the Huguang governor-general be transferred to Jingzhou, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 進吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 三年，拜保和殿大學士。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Preserving Harmony.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made Grand Secretary of the Hall of Preserving Harmony.

sentences.zh: 時輔臣柄政，論事輒爭執，裔介調和異同，時有所匡正。

translations.literal: At this time assisting ministers held power; discussing affairs they frequently disputed; Yijie harmonized differences and at times made corrections.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers then held real power and often quarreled over policy; Yijie mediated their disputes and sometimes corrected their course.

sentences.zh: 預修世祖實錄，充總裁官。

translations.literal: He took part in compiling the Veritable Records of the Shizu Emperor and served as chief editor.
translations.idiomatic: He helped compile the Veritable Records of the Shizu Emperor and served as chief editor.

sentences.zh: 九年，典會試。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he presided over the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he presided over the metropolitan civil service examination.

sentences.zh: 是年內院承旨會吏、禮二部選新進士六十人，試以文字，擬上中下三等入奏，上親定二十七人為庶吉士。

translations.literal: That year the Inner Court edict-drafter together with the Ministries of Personnel and Rites selected sixty new jinshi, tested them in writing, drafted upper, middle and lower grades for memorial, and the emperor personally fixed twenty-seven as Hanlin bachelors.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Inner Court drafter, together with the Ministries of Personnel and Rites, selected sixty new jinshi, tested their essays, and ranked them in three grades for the throne. The emperor personally chose twenty-seven as Hanlin bachelors.

sentences.zh: 御史李之芳劾裔介所擬上卷二十四人，先使人通信，招權納賄；

translations.literal: Censor Li Zhifang impeached Yijie: of the twenty-four men he placed in the upper grade, he first sent men to communicate, usurping power and accepting bribes;
translations.idiomatic: Censor Li Zhifang impeached Yijie, charging that of the twenty-four candidates he placed in the top grade, he had sent intermediaries ahead of time to trade influence for bribes;

sentences.zh: 並謂與班布爾善相比，引用私人。

translations.literal: and also said he was comparable to Banbu'ershan, employing private persons.
translations.idiomatic: and alleged that he had acted like Banbu'ershan in advancing his own men.

sentences.zh: 班布爾善官大學士，黨鼇拜，伏法。

translations.literal: Banbu'ershan held the office of Grand Secretary, factioned with Oboi, and was executed by law.
translations.idiomatic: Banbu'ershan had been a grand secretary, a partisan of Oboi, and was eventually executed.

sentences.zh: 上命裔介復奏，裔介疏辨，並言：「臣與班布爾善同官，論事輒齟《齒吾》。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Yijie to memorialize again; Yijie submitted a defense memorial, also saying: "Your servant and Banbu'ershan were colleagues; discussing affairs we frequently clashed in discord.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Yijie to reply in writing. Yijie defended himself, saying: "I served alongside Banbu'ershan, and whenever we discussed policy we were at odds.

sentences.zh: 以鼇拜之執焰，足跡不至其門，豈肯附班布爾善？

translations.literal: Because of Oboi's overbearing flame, my footsteps never reached his gate—how could I be willing to attach to Banbu'ershan?
translations.idiomatic: Because of Oboi's overbearing power I would not even set foot at his door—how then could I have sided with Banbu'ershan?

sentences.zh: 臣服官以來，彈劾無所避忌。

translations.literal: Since Your servant took office, in impeachment there has been no avoidance or taboo.
translations.idiomatic: Since I entered office I have impeached whomever duty required, without fear.

sentences.zh: 前劾劉正宗，其黨切齒於臣者十年於茲。

translations.literal: Earlier I impeached Liu Zhengzong; his faction has gnashed teeth at Your servant for ten years now.
translations.idiomatic: When I impeached Liu Zhengzong earlier, his faction has hated me for these ten years.

sentences.zh: 之芳，正宗同鄉，今為報復。」

translations.literal: Zhifang is a fellow townsman of Zhengzong; now he acts in revenge."
translations.idiomatic: Zhifang is Zhengzong's fellow townsman and now seeks revenge.

sentences.zh: 因自請罷斥，疏下吏部會質。

translations.literal: Thereupon he requested his own dismissal; the memorial was sent down to the Ministry of Personnel for joint examination.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked to be dismissed. The memorial was referred to the Ministry of Personnel for a joint inquiry.

sentences.zh: 之芳力爭，裔介自引咎。

translations.literal: Zhifang argued forcefully; Yijie took blame upon himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhifang pressed his case vigorously, while Yijie accepted blame himself.

sentences.zh: 部議以之芳劾奏有因，裔介應削秩罰俸，上寬之，命供職如故。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated that Zhifang's impeachment had grounds; Yijie should have rank reduced and salary fined; the emperor was lenient and ordered him to continue in office as before.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry ruled that Zhifang's charges had some basis and recommended reducing Yijie's rank and fining his salary, but the emperor was lenient and allowed him to remain in office.

sentences.zh: 十年，以老病乞休，詔許解官回籍。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, on account of age and illness he requested retirement; an edict permitted him to leave office and return to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he asked to retire on grounds of age and illness; the emperor allowed him to resign and return home.

sentences.zh: 世祖實錄成，進太子太傅。

translations.literal: When the Veritable Records of the Shizu Emperor were completed, he was advanced to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Veritable Records of the Shizu Emperor were completed, he was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，卒，賜祭葬如製。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he died; sacrificial rites and burial were granted according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he died, and the court granted him the prescribed funeral honors.

sentences.zh: 裔介居言路最久，疏至百餘上，敷陳剴切，多見施行。

translations.literal: Yijie held the avenue of speech longest; memorials reached more than a hundred; his presentations were earnest and incisive, and many were put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: Yijie served longest on the censorial path, submitting more than a hundred memorials. His arguments were earnest and sharp, and many of his proposals were adopted.

sentences.zh: 生平篤誠，信程、硃之學，以見知聞知述聖學之統。

translations.literal: Throughout his life he was sincere and devoted, believing in the learning of Cheng and Zhu, using seeing-and-knowing and hearing-and-knowing to expound the lineage of sagely learning.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout his life he was devout and sincere, devoted to the Cheng–Zhu school, and wrote to carry forward the orthodox transmission of the sages through the categories of innate knowing.

sentences.zh: 著述凡百餘卷，大指原本儒先，並及經世之學。

translations.literal: His writings altogether exceed a hundred juan; their main purport returns to the Confucian forebears and also touches learning for ordering the age.
translations.idiomatic: His writings totaled more than a hundred juan, grounded chiefly in the Confucian classics and forebears, and extending to statecraft as well.

sentences.zh: 家居十六年，躬課稼穡，循行阡陌，人不知其為故相也。

translations.literal: Living at home sixteen years, he personally supervised farming, walked the field paths, and people did not know he was a former chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: During sixteen years at home he personally oversaw the farm, walked the fields himself, and neighbors did not realize he had once been chief minister.

sentences.zh: 雍正間，祀賢良祠。

translations.literal: During the Yongzheng period he was enshrined in the Shrine of Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongzheng reign he was enshrined in the Shrine of Worthy Officials.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，追諡文毅。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he was posthumously given the temple name Wényì.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 1 (1736) he was posthumously honored with the temple name Wényì.

sentences.zh: 熊賜履，字敬修，湖北孝感人。

translations.literal: Xiong Cilü, styled Jingxiu, was a man of Xiaogan in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Cilü, whose style was Jingxiu, came from Xiaogan in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 順治十五年進士，選庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Shunzhi he became a jinshi, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 15 (1658) he passed the jinshi examination, was chosen as a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 典順天鄉試，遷國子監司業，進弘文院侍讀。

translations.literal: He presided over the Shuntian provincial examination, was transferred to Vice Director of Studies in the Directorate of Education, and advanced to Reader in the Hall of Broad Learning.
translations.idiomatic: He presided over the Shuntian provincial examination, became Vice Director of Studies at the Directorate of Education, and was promoted to Reader in the Hall of Broad Learning.

sentences.zh: 康熙六年，聖祖詔求直言。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kangxi the Sage Ancestor issued an edict seeking blunt speech.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 6 (1667) the emperor issued an edict calling for candid memorials.

sentences.zh: 時輔臣鼇拜專政，賜履上疏幾萬言，略謂：「民生困苦孔亟，私派倍於官徵，雜項浮於正額。

translations.literal: At this time assisting minister Oboi monopolized government; Cilü submitted a memorial of nearly ten thousand characters, summarily saying: "The people's livelihood is in extreme distress; private levies are double the official collections; miscellaneous items exceed the regular quota.
translations.idiomatic: Oboi then dominated the government. Cilü submitted a memorial of nearly ten thousand characters, stating in essence: "The people's livelihood is in desperate straits. Unauthorized surcharges are twice the official tax, and miscellaneous levies exceed the regular quota.

sentences.zh: 一旦水旱頻仍，蠲豁則吏收其實而民受其名，賑濟則官增其肥而民重其瘠。

translations.literal: Once floods and droughts come frequently, when remission is granted the clerks receive the reality while the people bear the name; when relief is given officials increase their fat while the people bear redoubled leanness.
translations.idiomatic: When floods and droughts strike in succession, remissions are swallowed by clerks while the people gain only the empty name of relief; relief funds fatten officials while the people grow leaner still.

sentences.zh: 然非獨守令之過也，上之有監司，又上之有督撫。

translations.literal: Yet this is not the fault of prefects and magistrates alone; above them are surveillance commissioners, and above them governors-general and governors.
translations.idiomatic: Yet this is not the fault of local magistrates alone. Above them stand the surveillance commissioners, and above them the governors and governors-general.

sentences.zh: 朝廷方責守令以廉，而上官實縱之以貪；

translations.literal: The court is just then charging prefects and magistrates with integrity, yet superior officials in fact indulge them in greed;
translations.idiomatic: The court demands integrity from magistrates, yet their superiors in practice indulge their greed;

sentences.zh: 方授守令以養民之職，而上官實課以厲民之行。

translations.literal: Just then they were appointing prefects and magistrates to the duty of nourishing the people, yet superior officials in fact imposed tasks that harshly burdened the people's conduct.
translations.idiomatic: The court had just entrusted prefects and magistrates with the duty of caring for the people, yet their superiors in practice drove them to exactions that oppressed the people.

sentences.zh: 故督撫廉則監司廉，守令亦不得不廉；

translations.literal: Therefore, when governors-general and governors were incorrupt, the surveillance commissioners were incorrupt, and prefects and magistrates also could not but be incorrupt;
translations.idiomatic: When governors and governors-general were upright, the intendants followed suit, and local magistrates had no choice but to be upright as well;

sentences.zh: 督撫貪則監司貪，守令亦不得不貪。

translations.literal: when governors-general and governors were greedy, the surveillance commissioners were greedy, and prefects and magistrates also could not but be greedy.
translations.idiomatic: when governors and governors-general were corrupt, the intendants grew corrupt too, and local magistrates could hardly remain honest.

sentences.zh: 此又理勢之必然者也。

translations.literal: This, too, is what reason and circumstance inevitably require.
translations.idiomatic: Such is the inevitable logic of the system.

sentences.zh: 伏乞甄別督撫，以民生苦樂為守令之賢否，以守令貪廉為督撫之優劣。

translations.literal: I humbly beg that governors-general and governors be distinguished and evaluated, taking the people's hardship or ease as the measure of a prefect's or magistrate's merit or fault, and taking the integrity or corruption of prefects and magistrates as the measure of a governor's or governor-general's superiority or inferiority.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly ask that governors and governors-general be carefully assessed: let the people's hardship or welfare judge the worth of local magistrates, and let magistrates' integrity or corruption judge the quality of their superiors.

sentences.zh: 督撫得人，守令亦得人矣。

translations.literal: If governors-general and governors are well chosen, prefects and magistrates will also be well chosen.
translations.idiomatic: Choose the right men for the provincial posts, and the right men will fill the local posts as well.

sentences.zh: 雖然，內臣者外臣之表也，本原之地則在朝廷。

translations.literal: Although inner officials are the model for outer officials, the root and source lie in the court.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials set the example for those in the provinces, but the source of the problem lies in the capital itself.

sentences.zh: 其大者尤在立綱陳紀、用人行政之間。

translations.literal: The greatest matters lie especially in establishing norms, setting forth regulations, appointing men, and administering affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Above all, it turns on establishing standards, codifying rules, choosing officials, and governing well.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷之可議者不止一端，擇其重且大者言之：一曰，政事極其紛更，而國體因之日傷也。

translations.literal: Now what is open to discussion at court is more than one matter; selecting those that are weighty and great, I speak of them thus: first, government affairs have become extremely changeable, and the body politic is thereby injured day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Much at court deserves debate; I will take up only the weightiest points. First, policy has grown endlessly unsettled, and the institutions of state suffer daily harm.

sentences.zh: 國家章程法度，不聞略加整頓，而急功喜事之人又從而意為更變，但知趨目前尺寸之利以便其私，而不知無窮之患已潛滋暗伏於其中。

translations.literal: The nation's statutes and laws are not heard to receive even slight rectification, yet men eager for quick success and fond of novelty further set their minds on making changes at will; they know only to pursue immediate petty profit for their private ends, and do not know that boundless calamity has already been secretly growing within.
translations.idiomatic: The empire's laws and institutions receive no real overhaul, while men hungry for quick results keep inventing new changes. They chase immediate gain for themselves, blind to the endless trouble quietly taking root.

sentences.zh: 乞敕議政王等詳議制度，參酌古今，勒為會典，則上有道揆、下有法守矣。

translations.literal: I beg that the regent princes and others be ordered to discuss the system in detail, weigh past and present, and compile it into an institutional code; then above there will be governing principles and below there will be laws to uphold.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the regent princes be commanded to review the system in full, weigh ancient and modern practice, and fix it in a formal code—so that those above have clear principles of rule and those below have fixed laws to follow.

sentences.zh: 一曰，職業極其隳窳，而士氣因之日靡也。

translations.literal: Second, official duties have fallen into extreme decay, and the morale of scholar-officials is thereby debilitated day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Second, official conduct has sunk to ruinous slackness, and the spirit of the bureaucracy withers by the day.

sentences.zh: 部院臣工大率緘默瞻顧，外託老成慎重之名，內懷持祿養身之念。

translations.literal: Ministers and officials of the ministries and courts are for the most part silent and watchful; outwardly they profess mature prudence, but inwardly they harbor the thought of holding their salaries and preserving themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Most ministers and court officials keep silent and look about them. They affect sober caution in public while privately clinging to their stipends and their own safety.

sentences.zh: 憂憤者謂之疏狂，任事者目為躁競，廉靜者斥為矯激，端方者詆為迂腐。

translations.literal: Those who were anxious and indignant were called reckless; those who took on affairs were regarded as rash and ambitious; the pure and quiet were denounced as artificially extreme; the upright were slandered as pedantic and stale.
translations.idiomatic: The anxious were labeled wild, the conscientious branded as pushy, the restrained dismissed as affected, and the upright mocked as hidebound.

sentences.zh: 間有讀書窮理之士，則群指為道學，誹笑詆排，欲禁錮其終身而後已。

translations.literal: Occasionally there were scholars who read books and exhaustively investigated principle; then all would point to them as adherents of the Way Learning, ridicule and vilify them, and wish to imprison them for life before they would stop.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a scholar truly pursued learning and moral principle, the rest would cry 'Neo-Confucian!'—mocking and attacking him until they could see him ruined for good.

sentences.zh: 乞申飭滿、漢諸臣，虛衷酌理，實心任事，化情面為肝膽，轉推諉為擔當。

translations.literal: I beg that Manchu and Han officials be instructed and admonished to open their minds and weigh reason, to take up affairs in earnest, to transform personal favor into loyal forthrightness, and to turn shirking into bearing responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Manchu and Han officials alike be charged to think openly, serve sincerely, replace favor-trading with honest counsel, and turn evasion into responsibility.

sentences.zh: 漢官勿阿附滿官，堂官勿偏任司員。

translations.literal: Han officials should not fawn upon Manchu officials, and department heads should not show partial favor toward their section members.
translations.idiomatic: Han officials must not curry favor with Manchu colleagues, nor may department heads play favorites among their subordinates.

sentences.zh: 宰執盡心獻納，勿以唯諾為休容，臺諫極力糾繩，勿以鉗結為將順，則職業修舉，官箴日肅而士氣日奮矣。

translations.literal: Let the chief ministers offer advice with all their heart and not treat mere assent as accommodation; let the censorate and remonstrators censure with all their strength and not treat muzzling as going along—then official duties will be maintained, official integrity will grow daily strict, and morale will rise daily.
translations.idiomatic: Let the grand secretaries speak their minds rather than treat compliance as courtesy; let the censors and remonstrators press their cases rather than treat silence as deference. Then duties will be properly performed, official discipline restored, and the spirit of service revived.

sentences.zh: 一曰，學校極其廢弛，而文教因之日衰也。

translations.literal: Third, the schools have fallen into extreme neglect, and culture and education are thereby declining day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Third, the schools have collapsed into neglect, and learning and moral instruction decay with each passing day.

sentences.zh: 今庠序之教缺焉不講，師道不立，經訓不明。

translations.literal: Now instruction in the schools is wholly neglected and undiscussed; the teacher's way is not established, and the classical teachings are not clear.
translations.idiomatic: School instruction is scarcely given at all. The authority of teachers has vanished, and the meaning of the classics is lost.

sentences.zh: 士子惟揣摩舉業，為弋科名掇富貴之具，不知讀書講學、求聖賢理道之歸。

translations.literal: Scholars only study and refine examination essays as tools to pursue examination honors and grasp wealth and rank; they do not know how to read books, lecture, and seek the goal of the sages' and worthies' principles and the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Students care only to polish their examination essays—the means to win degrees and fortune—and no longer read, debate, or seek the wisdom of the sages.

sentences.zh: 高明者或汎濫於百家，沉淪於二氏，斯道淪晦，未有甚於此時者也。

translations.literal: The bright sometimes drift broadly among the hundred schools or sink into the Two Teachings; the Way has grown dark—never worse than at this time.
translations.idiomatic: The ablest wander lost among rival schools or drown in Buddhism and Daoism. The true Way has never been so obscured.

sentences.zh: 乞責成學院、學道，統率士子，講明正學，特簡儒臣使司成均，則道術以明，教化大行，人才日出矣。

translations.literal: I beg that provincial education commissioners be charged to lead the scholars, to elucidate orthodox learning, and that Confucian ministers be specially selected to administer the Directorate of Education; then the Way and its arts will be clarified, great teaching will be broadly practiced, and talent will emerge day by day.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that provincial education officers be made responsible for guiding students in orthodox learning, and that distinguished Confucian scholars be appointed to head the Directorate of Education. Then the Way will be clear, instruction will flourish, and capable men will appear in steady succession.

sentences.zh: 一曰，風俗極其僭濫，而禮制因之日壞也。

translations.literal: Fourth, customs have become extremely extravagant and overstepping, and the ritual system is thereby deteriorating day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, public morals have grown wildly extravagant, and ritual propriety breaks down daily.

sentences.zh: 今一裘而費中人之產，一宴而糜終歲之糧，輿隸被貴介之服，倡優擬命婦之飾，習為固然。

translations.literal: Now one fur coat costs a middle-class family's entire property; one feast consumes a year's grain; cart attendants wear the dress of noble scions; actors and singers imitate the ornaments of officials' wives—and all this is taken as natural.
translations.idiomatic: A single coat may ruin a middling household; a single feast may devour a year's grain. Servants dress like gentlemen; players ape the finery of officials' wives—and no one thinks it strange.

sentences.zh: 夫風俗奢、禮制壞，為飢寒之本原，盜賊、訟獄、兇荒所由起也。

translations.literal: When customs are extravagant and the ritual system is broken, this is the root of hunger and cold, and the source from which bandits, lawsuits, and famine arise.
translations.idiomatic: Luxury and the ruin of ritual are the wellspring of hunger and want, and the breeding ground of crime, litigation, and famine.

sentences.zh: 乞明詔內外臣民，一以儉約為尚，自王公以及士庶，凡宮室、車馬、衣服，規定經制，不許逾越，則貪風自息、民俗漸醇矣。

translations.literal: I beg that a clear edict be issued to officials and people within and without, all taking frugality as what is honored; from princes and dukes down to commoners, for palaces, carriages, horses, and clothing alike, fixed standards should be prescribed and transgression not permitted—then the wind of greed will cease of itself and folk customs will gradually grow pure.
translations.idiomatic: I ask for a clear decree enjoining frugality on all, from princes to commoners, with fixed limits on houses, carriages, horses, and dress beyond which none may go. Greed will then subside, and custom will slowly recover its sobriety.

sentences.zh: 雖然，猶非本計也。

translations.literal: Although this is so, it is still not the fundamental plan.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, this is not yet the root remedy.

sentences.zh: 根本切要，端在皇上。

translations.literal: The fundamental and critical point lies with Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: The decisive matter rests with the emperor himself.

sentences.zh: 皇上生長深宮，春秋方富，正宜慎選左右，輔導聖躬，薰陶德性，優以保衡之任，隆以師傅之禮；

translations.literal: Your Majesty grew up in the deep palace; your years are still abundant. It is precisely fitting to choose carefully those at your side to guide your sacred person, to cultivate your moral nature, to honor them with a regent's responsibility, and to treat them with a master's rites;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty was raised within the palace walls and is still young. This is the time to choose your companions with care—men who can guide you, shape your character, serve you as guardians, and be honored as your teachers;

sentences.zh: 又妙選天下英俊，使之陪侍法從，朝夕獻納。

translations.literal: and also to select outstanding men from throughout the realm, causing them to attend as companions in the imperial retinue and to offer advice morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: and to gather the finest talent in the empire to attend you, offering counsel from dawn till dusk.

sentences.zh: 毋徒事講幄之虛文，毋徒應經筵之故事，毋以寒暑有輟，毋以晨夕有間。

translations.literal: Do not merely perform the empty form of the lectern sessions; do not merely observe the old routine of the classics mat; do not pause for cold or heat; do not leave gaps between morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: Do not reduce study to empty ceremony, nor treat the classics mat as mere precedent. Let neither season nor hour interrupt it.

sentences.zh: 於是考諸六經之文，監於歷代之跡，實體諸身心，以為敷政出治之本。

translations.literal: Thereupon examine the texts of the Six Classics, observe the tracks of past dynasties, embody them in body and mind, and take this as the foundation for spreading governance and issuing rule.
translations.idiomatic: Study the Six Classics, weigh the lessons of history, and make them part of your own person—the foundation from which all government must proceed.

sentences.zh: 若夫左右近習，必端其選，綴衣虎賁，亦擇其人。

translations.literal: As for those close attendants and familiar favorites, their selection must be upright; robe attendants and imperial guards must also be chosen for their persons.
translations.idiomatic: Those nearest you must be chosen with strict care—even attendants of the robe and the imperial guard must be men of worth.

sentences.zh: 佞幸不置於前，聲色不禦於側。

translations.literal: Flatterers should not be placed before you; music and beauty should not be kept at your side.
translations.idiomatic: Let no sycophant stand before you, and let no pleasure of sound or color attend your side.

sentences.zh: 非聖之書不讀，無益之事不為。

translations.literal: Books that are not the sages' should not be read; things that are not beneficial should not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Read nothing that is not the word of the sages; do nothing that does not serve the good.

sentences.zh: 內而深宮燕閒之間，外而大廷廣眾之地，微而起居言動之恆，凡所以維持此身者無不備，防閒此心者無不周，主德清明，君身強固。

translations.literal: Within, in the leisure of the deep palace; without, in the broad assembly of the great court; in the subtle constancy of daily rising, resting, speaking, and acting—everything by which this person is maintained should be complete, and everything by which this mind is guarded should be thorough; then sovereign virtue will be clear and bright, and the sovereign person strong and secure.
translations.idiomatic: In private within the palace and in public before the court alike; in the smallest habits of daily life—leave nothing undone that sustains the person, nothing neglected that guards the mind. Then your virtue will shine clear and your person stand firm.

sentences.zh: 由是直接二帝三王之心法，目足措斯世於唐、虞、三代之盛，又何吏治之不清，民生之不遂哉？」

translations.literal: Thereby you may directly connect with the heart-methods of the Two Emperors and Three Kings, and your eyes will suffice to place this age in the prosperity of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties—what worry that official governance should not be clear, or that the people's livelihood should not be fulfilled?"
translations.idiomatic: Then you may inherit the wisdom of the sage-kings of antiquity and bring this age to the glory of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties. What cause would remain to fear bad government or an unhappy people?

sentences.zh: 疏入，鼇拜惡之，請治以妄言罪，上勿許。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted. Oboi hated it and requested that he be punished for the crime of reckless speech, but the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted. Oboi resented it and asked that Xiong Cilü be punished for reckless speech, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 七年，遷秘書院侍讀學士。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he was transferred to Reader Bachelor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, he was promoted to Reader Bachelor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「朝政積習未除，國計隱憂可慮。

translations.literal: In a memorial he said: "Accumulated habits of court governance have not been removed, and hidden worries for the nation's planning are cause for concern.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Old abuses at court remain unremoved, and hidden dangers to the state give cause for alarm.

sentences.zh: 年來災異頻仍，飢荒疊見，正宵旰憂勤、徹懸減膳之日，講學勤政，在今日最為切要。

translations.literal: In recent years calamities and anomalies have come repeatedly, and famine has appeared again and again. This is precisely the time for worrying through the night, suspending the bell, and reducing meals; to study and govern diligently is today most urgently needed.
translations.idiomatic: Disasters have struck again and again, and famine has followed in succession. This is the very hour when the emperor should rise early and eat sparingly in anxious care. Study and diligent governance are now more urgent than ever.

sentences.zh: 乞時禦便殿，接見群臣，講求政治，行之以誠，持之以敬，庶幾轉咎徵為休徵。」

translations.literal: I beg that Your Majesty from time to time hold court in the convenient hall, receive and see the assembled ministers, discuss and seek good governance, carry it out with sincerity, and maintain it with reverence, so that perhaps omens of blame may be turned into omens of blessing.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty hold audience from time to time in the side hall, meet your ministers face to face, and earnestly discuss the business of government—with sincerity in action and reverence in constancy—so that ill omens may give way to good.

sentences.zh: 疏入，鼇拜傳旨詰問積習、隱憂實事，以所陳無據，妄奏沽名，下吏議，鐫二秩，上原之。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted. Oboi transmitted an imperial order questioning him about the concrete facts behind the accumulated habits and hidden worries; because what he had stated lacked evidence and he had recklessly memorialized to seek fame, the case was sent to the officials for deliberation and he was reduced two ranks, but the emperor pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted. Oboi relayed an imperial demand for specifics on those old abuses and hidden dangers. Finding his charges unsupported and his purpose self-promoting, the authorities recommended demoting him two ranks; the emperor spared him.

sentences.zh: 八年，鼇拜敗，命康親王杰書等鞫治，以鼇拜銜賜履，意圖傾害，為罪狀之一。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Oboi fell. The Kangxi Emperor ordered Prince Kang Jieshu and others to investigate and try the case, and Oboi's grudge against Xiong Cilü and intent to harm him were made one of the counts in the indictment.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, Oboi was overthrown. Prince Kang Jieshu and others were ordered to investigate him, and among the charges listed was his grudge against Xiong Cilü and his attempt to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 方鼇拜輔政擅威福，大臣稍與異同，立加誅戮。

translations.literal: When Oboi assisted in government and monopolized power and favor, if a great minister showed even slight disagreement, execution was immediately added.
translations.idiomatic: While Oboi held power, any senior minister who dared disagree even slightly was promptly put to death.

sentences.zh: 賜履以詞臣論事侃侃無所避，用是著直聲。

translations.literal: Xiong Cilü, as a literary official, discussed affairs frankly and without avoidance, and thereby gained a reputation for forthrightness.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Cilü spoke out boldly on public affairs without flinching, and so won a name for plainspoken integrity.

sentences.zh: 上即位後，未舉經筵，賜履特具疏請之，並請設起居注官。

translations.literal: After the emperor had ascended the throne, the classics mat had not yet been instituted. Xiong Cilü specially submitted a memorial requesting it, and also requested the establishment of Diary Keeper offices.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor's accession, the classics lectures had not yet been restored. Xiong Cilü memorialized specifically to request them, and also asked that Diary Keeper posts be established.

sentences.zh: 上欲幸塞外，以賜履疏諫，乃寢，且嘉其直。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to visit the region beyond the passes. Xiong Cilü remonstrated in a memorial, and the plan was then abandoned; the emperor moreover praised his frankness.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor planned a journey beyond the Great Wall, Xiong Cilü dissuaded him by memorial. The tour was dropped, and the emperor commended his candor.

sentences.zh: 九年，擢國史院學士。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he was promoted to Bachelor of the History Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, he was promoted to Bachelor of the History Academy.

sentences.zh: 未幾，复內閣，設翰林院，更以為掌院學士。

translations.literal: Before long, the Grand Secretariat was restored and the Hanlin Academy established; he was again appointed Chancellor of the Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Grand Secretariat was restored and the Hanlin Academy established; he was again made Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 舉經筵，以賜履為講官，日進講弘德殿。

translations.literal: When the classics mat was instituted, Xiong Cilü was made lecturer and daily lectured in the Hall of Expanding Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: When the classics lectures began, Xiong Cilü served as lecturer, delivering daily instruction in the Hall of Expanding Virtue.

sentences.zh: 賜履上陳道德，下達民隱，上每虛己以聽。

translations.literal: Xiong Cilü expounded moral principle above and conveyed the people's hidden grievances below; the emperor each time emptied himself to listen.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Cilü spoke of moral principle to the throne and brought up the people's hidden troubles below; the emperor always listened with an open mind.

sentences.zh: 十四年，諭★其才能清慎，遷內閣學士，尋超授武英殿大學士，兼刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, an edict commended his ability as pure and cautious; he was transferred to Grand Secretariat Bachelor, and soon was exceptionally appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Military Glory, concurrently serving as Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, the emperor commended his ability as pure and cautious, promoted him to Grand Secretariat Bachelor, and soon elevated him directly to Grand Secretary of the Hall of Military Glory while also appointing him Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 十五年，陝西總督哈佔疏報獲盜，開復疏防官，下內閣，賜履誤票三法司核擬。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, Shaanxi Governor-General Hazhan memorialized reporting the capture of bandits and the restoration of negligent defense officials. The memorial was sent to the Grand Secretariat, and Xiong Cilü mistakenly endorsed it for review by the Three Judicial Offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, Shaanxi Governor-General Hazhan reported the capture of bandits and the reinstatement of negligent frontier officers. When the memorial reached the Grand Secretariat, Xiong Cilü wrongly endorsed it for review by the Three Judicial Offices.

sentences.zh: 既，檢舉，得旨免究。

translations.literal: Afterward it was investigated and reported, and an imperial order was received exempting him from inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was later investigated, and an edict arrived excusing him from punishment.

sentences.zh: 賜履改草簽，欲諉咎同官杜立德，又取原草簽嚼而毀之，立德以語索額圖。

translations.literal: Xiong Cilü altered the draft endorsement, wishing to shift blame onto his colleague Du Lede; he again took the original draft endorsement, chewed it, and destroyed it. Lede told Suo'etu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Cilü changed the draft endorsement, trying to blame his colleague Du Lede, then retrieved the original draft, chewed it up, and destroyed it. Du Lede reported this to Suo'etu.

sentences.zh: 事上聞，吏部議賜履票擬錯誤，欲諉咎同官杜立德，改寫草簽，复私取嚼毀，失大臣體，坐奪官。

translations.literal: When the matter reached the emperor, the Ministry of Personnel deliberated that Xiong Cilü's endorsement was mistaken, that he wished to shift blame onto his colleague Du Lede, that he altered the draft endorsement and again privately took and chewed it to destroy it, and that he lost the dignity proper to a great minister; he was sentenced to deprivation of office.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned of it, the Ministry of Personnel ruled that Xiong Cilü had erred in his endorsement, tried to blame Du Lede, altered the draft, and secretly destroyed it by chewing—conduct unworthy of a senior minister. He was stripped of his post.

sentences.zh: 歸，僑居江寧。

translations.literal: He returned home and lived in exile at Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: He went home and lived in retirement at Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，上南巡，賜履迎謁，召入對，御書經義齋榜以賜。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, when the emperor made a southern tour, Xiong Cilü came out to greet and pay homage; he was summoned for an audience, and the emperor's own brush wrote the plaque for the Jingyi Studio to bestow upon him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, during the emperor's southern tour, Xiong Cilü came forward to greet him, was summoned to audience, and received an imperial inscription for the Jingyi Studio written in the emperor's own hand.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，起禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, he was recalled as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year, he was recalled to serve as Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以母憂去。

translations.literal: Before long, he left office on account of mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he left office to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，上复南巡，賞賚有加。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, when the emperor again made a southern tour, rewards and gifts to him were increased.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year, on the emperor's second southern tour, he received additional gifts and honors.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，起故官，仍直經筵。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, he was recalled to his former office and again attended the classics mat.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year, he was restored to his former post and again attended the classics lectures.

sentences.zh: 命往江南讞獄，調吏部。

translations.literal: He was ordered to go to Jiangnan to judge criminal cases and was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to Jiangnan to hear criminal cases and was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 會河督靳輔請豁近河所佔民田額賦，命賜履會勘。

translations.literal: When River Commissioner Jin Fu requested exemption of the tax quota on farmland occupied near the river, the emperor ordered Xiong Cilü to join in the investigation.
translations.idiomatic: When River Commissioner Jin Fu asked that tax quotas be remitted on farmland taken by the river, the emperor ordered Xiong Cilü to investigate jointly with him.

sentences.zh: 奏免高郵、山陽等州縣額賦三千七百二十八頃有奇。

translations.literal: He memorialized exemption of the tax quota for Gaoyou, Shanyang, and other prefectures and counties, amounting to three thousand seven hundred twenty-eight qing and a fraction.
translations.idiomatic: He reported remission of tax quotas on 3,728-odd qing of land in Gaoyou, Shanyang, and other counties.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，弟編修賜瓚以奏對欺飾下獄，御史龔翔麟遂劾吏部銓除州縣以意高下，賜履偽學欺罔，乞嚴譴。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year, his younger brother, Compiler Xiong Cizan, was imprisoned for deceptive answers at court audience. Censor Gong Xianglin then impeached the Ministry of Personnel for appointing prefectures and counties arbitrarily high or low, and charged that Xiong Cilü's false learning and deception merited severe punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year, his younger brother, Compiler Xiong Cizan, was jailed for deceitful answers at court. Censor Gong Xianglin then impeached the Ministry of Personnel for manipulating county appointments and accused Xiong Cilü of hypocritical learning and deception, demanding severe punishment.

sentences.zh: 下都察院議，賜履與尚書庫勒納，侍郎趙士麟、彭孫遹當降官，上不問，賜瓚亦獲赦。

translations.literal: The case was sent to the Censorate for deliberation. Xiong Cilü and Minister Kule Na, and Vice Ministers Zhao Shilin and Peng Sunyu, should have been demoted in rank, but the emperor did not pursue the matter, and Cizan also obtained pardon.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate recommended demotion for Xiong Cilü, Minister Kule Na, and Vice Ministers Zhao Shilin and Peng Sunyu, but the emperor took no action, and Cizan was also pardoned.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，授東閣大學士兼吏部尚書，預修聖訓、實錄、方略、明史，並充總裁官。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year, he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, concurrently Minister of Personnel; he participated in compiling the Imperial Instructions, Veritable Records, Strategic Accounts, and History of Ming, and also served as chief compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-eighth year, he was made Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion and Minister of Personnel. He helped compile the Imperial Instructions, Veritable Records, Strategic Accounts, and History of Ming, serving as chief editor.

sentences.zh: 典會試者五。

translations.literal: He presided over the metropolitan examination five times.
translations.idiomatic: He administered the metropolitan examination five times.

sentences.zh: 以年老累疏乞休。

translations.literal: Because of old age he repeatedly memorialized requesting retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Age led him to memorialize repeatedly for retirement.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，溫旨許解機務，仍食俸，留京備顧問。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year, a gracious edict permitted him to leave state affairs; he still received salary and remained in the capital as a consultant.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year, a warm edict allowed him to withdraw from active duty while keeping his stipend and remaining in the capital as an adviser.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，乞歸江寧。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year, he requested leave to return to Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fifth year, he asked permission to return to Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 比行，召入講論累日。

translations.literal: As he was about to depart, he was summoned to enter and discuss matters for many days.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of his departure, the emperor summoned him for days of conversation.

sentences.zh: 賜履因奏巡幸所至，官民供張煩費，惟上留意，上頷之，給傳遣官護歸。

translations.literal: Xiong Cilü then memorialized that wherever imperial tours went, the provisioning by officials and people was troublesome and costly, and asked only that the emperor take heed; the emperor nodded, granted post horses, and dispatched an official to escort him home.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Cilü then observed that imperial tours burdened officials and people with costly preparations, and asked the emperor to bear it in mind. The emperor nodded assent, gave him traveling horses, and sent an official to escort him home.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，上閱河，幸江寧，召見慰問，賜御用冠服。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year, when the emperor inspected the rivers and visited Jiangning, he summoned Xiong Cilü, consoled him, and bestowed upon him an imperial hat and robe for personal use.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-sixth year, while inspecting the rivers and visiting Jiangning, the emperor summoned Xiong Cilü, comforted him, and granted him an imperial cap and robe.

sentences.zh: 四十八年，卒，年七十五，命禮部遣官視喪，賜賻金千兩，贈太子太保，諡文端。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year, he died at the age of seventy-five. The Ministry of Rites was ordered to dispatch officials to oversee the funeral; he was granted one thousand taels of condolence money, posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Protector of the Crown Prince, and given the posthumous title Wenduan.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-eighth year he died at seventy-five. The Ministry of Rites was ordered to oversee his funeral. He received a thousand taels of condolence money, was posthumously honored as Grand Protector of the Crown Prince, and given the posthumous name Wenduan.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，上追念賜履，知其貧，迭命江寧織造周恤其家，諭吏部召其二子志契、志夔詣京師，皆尚幼，复諭賜履僚屬門生醵金佽之。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year, the emperor recalled Xiong Cilü, knew that he had been poor, and repeatedly ordered the Jiangning Weaving Bureau to relieve his family; he instructed the Ministry of Personnel to summon his two sons, Zhiji and Zhikui, to the capital. Both were still young, and he again instructed Xiong Cilü's colleagues and students to contribute money to assist them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-first year, remembering Xiong Cilü and knowing how poor his household was, the emperor repeatedly ordered the Jiangning Weaving Bureau to support his family, commanded the Ministry of Personnel to summon his sons Zhiji and Zhikui to the capital—they were still young—and asked Xiong Cilü's colleagues and students to raise funds for their upkeep.

sentences.zh: 賜履論學，以默識篤行為旨，其言曰：「聖賢之道，不外乎庸，庸乃所以為神也。」

translations.literal: In discussing learning, Xiong Cilü took silent recognition and earnest conduct as his aim. His words were: "The Way of the sages and worthies is nothing outside the commonplace; the commonplace is precisely how it becomes divine.
translations.idiomatic: In his teaching, Xiong Cilü held that true learning lay in quiet understanding and steadfast action. He said: "The Way of the sages is nothing but the ordinary; it is through the ordinary that the divine is reached.

sentences.zh: 著閒道錄，嘗進上，命備省覽。

translations.literal: He authored the Records of the Idle Way, once presented it to the emperor, and was ordered to keep it for imperial review.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Records of the Idle Way, presented it to the throne, and was told to keep a copy for the emperor's reading.

sentences.zh: 雍正間，祀賢良祠。

translations.literal: During the Yongzheng reign, he was enshrined in the Temple of Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongzheng period he was enshrined in the Temple of Worthies.

sentences.zh: 李光地，字晉卿，福建安溪人。

translations.literal: Li Guangdi, styled Jinqing, was a native of Anxi in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangdi, whose style was Jinqing, came from Anxi in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 幼穎異。

translations.literal: In youth he was unusually bright.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he showed exceptional talent.

sentences.zh: 年十三，舉家陷山賊中，得脫歸。

translations.literal: At the age of thirteen, his whole family fell into the hands of mountain bandits, but he escaped and returned.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen his whole family was seized by mountain brigands; he alone escaped and made his way home.

sentences.zh: 力學慕古。

translations.literal: He strove in learning and admired antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: He studied hard and looked to the examples of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 康熙九年成進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kangxi he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 9 (1670) he passed the jinshi examination, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 十二年，乞省親歸。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, he requested leave to visit his parents and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he asked leave to visit his parents and went home.

sentences.zh: 十三年，耿精忠反，鄭錦據泉州，光地奉親匿山谷間，錦與精忠並遣人招之，力拒。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Geng Jingzhong rebelled and Zheng Jing held Quanzhou. Li Guangdi hid with his parents in the mountain valleys. Both Jing and Jingzhong sent men to recruit him, but he forcefully refused.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, Geng Jingzhong rose in rebellion and Zheng Jing seized Quanzhou. Li Guangdi concealed his parents in the hills. Both rebels sent envoys to win him over, but he steadfastly refused.

sentences.zh: 十四年，密疏言：「閩疆褊小，自二賊割據，誅求敲撲，民力已盡，賊勢亦窮。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, in a secret memorial he said: "The Fujian frontier is narrow and small. Since the two rebels carved out territory, extortion and beating have exhausted the people's strength, and the rebels' power is also at an end.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he sent a secret memorial: "Fujian is a small province. Under the two rebels' rule, endless exactions have drained the people, and the rebels themselves are nearing collapse.

sentences.zh: 南來大兵宜急攻，不可假以歲月，恐生他變。

translations.literal: The great army coming from the south should attack urgently and cannot be given months and years, for fear that other changes may arise.
translations.idiomatic: The southern expedition should strike at once. To delay even a few months risks fresh trouble.

sentences.zh: 方今精忠悉力於仙霞、杉關，鄭錦並命於漳、潮之界，惟汀州小路與贛州接壤，賊所置守禦不過千百疲卒。

translations.literal: At present Jingzhong is exerting all his strength at Xianxia and Shanguan, and Zheng Jing is likewise deploying troops on the Zhangzhou and Chaozhou border. Only the small path at Tingzhou adjoins Ganzhou, and the garrisons the rebels have posted there are no more than a thousand or so weary soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Jingzhong now concentrates his forces at Xianxia and Shanguan, while Zheng Jing mass troops on the Zhangzhou-Chaozhou line. Only the Tingzhou trail, bordering Ganzhou, is held by a mere thousand exhausted men.

sentences.zh: 竊聞大兵南來，皆於賊兵多處鏖戰，而不知出奇以搗其虛，此計之失也。

translations.literal: I have privately heard that when the great army comes south, it always fights pitched battles where rebel troops are numerous, and does not know to use a surprise stroke against their emptiness—this is the failure of the plan.
translations.idiomatic: I understand the main army always engages where rebel numbers are greatest, never striking where they are weak. That is the flaw in the strategy.

sentences.zh: 宜因賊防之疏，選精兵萬人或五六千人，詐為入廣，由贛達汀，為程七八日耳。

translations.literal: One should take advantage of the rebels' sparse defenses, select ten thousand elite troops or five or six thousand, feign an advance into Guangdong, and go from Ganzhou to Tingzhou—a journey of only seven or eight days.
translations.idiomatic: Exploit their thin defenses: send ten thousand picked men, or five or six thousand, feigning a march into Guangdong by way of Ganzhou to Tingzhou—a march of no more than seven or eight days.

sentences.zh: 二賊聞急趨救，非月餘不至，則我軍入閩久矣。

translations.literal: When the two rebels hear of the emergency and rush to the rescue, more than a month will pass before they arrive, and our army will long since have entered Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Both rebels would hurry to the rescue, but could not arrive in less than a month—by which time our forces would already be deep in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 賊方悉兵外拒，內地空虛，大軍果從汀州小路橫貫其腹，則三路之賊不戰自潰。

translations.literal: The rebels will just then have exhausted their troops in outward resistance, and the interior will be empty. If the great army truly crosses through their belly along the Tingzhou small path, then the rebels on all three routes will collapse without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: With their armies drawn outward and the interior bare, a thrust along the Tingzhou trail would cut straight through their center—and the rebel forces on all three fronts would crumble without a battle.

sentences.zh: 伏乞密敕領兵官偵諜虛實，隨機進取。

translations.literal: I humbly beg that commanding officers be secretly ordered to spy out emptiness and fullness and advance or seize according to opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly ask that field commanders be secretly instructed to reconnoiter enemy strength and act as occasion allows.

sentences.zh: 仍恐小路崎嶇，須使鄉兵在大軍之前，步兵又在馬兵之前，庶幾萬全，可以必勝。」

translations.literal: I still fear the small path is rugged; local militia must be placed before the great army, and infantry before cavalry—then perhaps all will be secure and victory can be assured.
translations.idiomatic: The trail is rough; local guides and militia should march ahead of the main force, with foot soldiers leading the cavalry. Only then will the plan be safe and victory certain.

sentences.zh: 置疏蠟丸中，遣使間道赴京師，因內閣學士富鴻基上之。

translations.literal: He placed the memorial in a wax pellet, sent a messenger by a secret route to the capital, and had it presented through Grand Secretariat Bachelor Fu Hongji.
translations.idiomatic: He sealed the memorial in a wax ball, sent a courier by hidden route to the capital, and had Grand Secretariat Bachelor Fu Hongji present it.

sentences.zh: 上得疏動容，嘉其忠，下兵部錄付領兵大臣。

translations.literal: When the emperor received the memorial, his expression changed; he praised Li Guangdi's loyalty and sent it down to the Ministry of War to copy and deliver to the commanding great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was visibly moved when he read it, praised Li Guangdi's loyalty, and ordered the Ministry of War to copy the memorial and forward it to the field commanders.

sentences.zh: 時尚之信亦叛，師次贛州、南安，未能入福建。

translations.literal: At that time Shang Zhixin also rebelled; the army halted at Ganzhou and Nan'an and could not enter Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: About then Shang Zhixin rebelled as well, and the imperial army stopped at Ganzhou and Nan'an, unable to push into Fujian.

sentences.zh: 康親王杰書自衢州克仙霞關，復建寧、延平，精忠請降。

translations.literal: Prince Kang Jieshu, advancing from Quzhou, captured Xianxia Pass, recovered Jianning and Yanping, and Jingzhong requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Kang Jieshu marched from Quzhou, took Xianxia Pass, recaptured Jianning and Yanping, and Geng Jingzhong sued for peace.

sentences.zh: 師進駐福州，令都統拉哈達、賚塔等討鄭錦，並求光地所在。

translations.literal: The army advanced and encamped at Fuzhou, ordering commanders-in-chief Lahada, Ledah, and others to campaign against Zheng Jing, and also to seek Guangdi's whereabouts.
translations.idiomatic: The army entered Fuzhou and ordered the commanders-in-chief Lahada, Ledah, and others to pursue Zheng Jing while searching for Li Guangdi.
