sentences.zh: 十六年，复泉州，光地謁拉哈達於漳州。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Quanzhou was recovered; Guangdi paid his respects to Lahada at Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, after Quanzhou was retaken, Li Guangdi went to Zhangzhou to call on Lahada.

sentences.zh: 拉哈達白王，疏稱「光地矢志為國，顛沛不渝，宜予褒揚」，命優敘，擢侍讀學士。

translations.literal: Lahada reported to the prince and submitted a memorial stating, "Guangdi is steadfast in devotion to the state and unwavering amid hardship; he should be commended and rewarded," and the court ordered special commendation and promoted him to Reader-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Lahada informed the prince and memorialized that Li Guangdi "has kept his heart fixed on the state through every trial and never wavered; he deserves praise and reward." The throne ordered him specially commended and promoted him to Hanlin Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 行至福州，以父喪歸。

translations.literal: When he reached Fuzhou he returned home on account of his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: He had only reached Fuzhou when he went home to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 十七年，同安賊蔡寅結眾萬餘，以白巾為號，掠安溪。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year the bandit Cai Yin of Tong'an gathered a force of more than ten thousand, took white turbans as their sign, and plundered Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, the Tong'an rebel Cai Yin mustered more than ten thousand men, rallied under white headcloths, and raided Anxi.

sentences.zh: 光地募鄉勇百餘人扼守，絕其糧道，賊解去。

translations.literal: Guangdi recruited more than a hundred local militiamen to hold them off, cut off their grain route, and the bandits dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangdi raised a little over a hundred local fighters to block them, severed their supply lines, and the rebels broke off the attack.

sentences.zh: 未幾，錦遣其將劉國軒陷海澄、漳平、同安、惠安諸縣，進逼泉州，斷萬安、江東二橋，南北援絕。

translations.literal: Before long Jing sent his general Liu Guoxuan to seize Haicheng, Zhangping, Tong'an, Hui'an, and other counties, pressed toward Quanzhou, severed the Wan'an and Jiangdong bridges, and cut off aid from north and south.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Zheng Jing sent his general Liu Guoxuan to overrun Haicheng, Zhangping, Tong'an, Hui'an, and the other counties, advance on Quanzhou, and destroy the Wan'an and Jiangdong bridges, isolating the city from relief on every side.

sentences.zh: 光地遣使赴拉哈達軍告急，值江水漲，道阻，乃導軍自漳平、安谿小道入。

translations.literal: Guangdi sent envoys to Lahada's army to report the emergency; the rivers were swollen and the roads blocked, so he guided the army in by the small paths through Zhangping and Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangdi dispatched messengers to Lahada's camp for help; when floodwaters blocked the main routes, he led the troops in by the back trails through Zhangping and Anxi.

sentences.zh: 光地從父日蠁率鄉勇度石珠嶺，芟荊棘，架浮橋以濟。

translations.literal: Guangdi's uncle Ri Xiang led local militia over Shizhu Ridge, cleared thorns and brambles, and built a pontoon bridge to cross.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangdi's uncle Ri Xiang took local militia over Shizhu Ridge, cut through the brush, and threw a pontoon bridge across the stream.

sentences.zh: 光地出迎，具牛酒犒軍。

translations.literal: Guangdi went out to meet them and provided cattle and wine to reward the army.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangdi went out to welcome them and furnished oxen and wine to feast the troops.

sentences.zh: 又使弟光垤、光垠以鄉兵千度白鴿嶺，迎巡撫吳興祚軍於永春。

translations.literal: He also sent his younger brothers Guangya and Guangyin with a thousand local troops over Baige Ridge to welcome Governor Wu Xingzuo's army at Yongchun.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent his brothers Guangya and Guangyin with a thousand local soldiers over Baige Ridge to meet Governor Wu Xingzuo's force at Yongchun.

sentences.zh: 師次泉州，擊破國軒，竄入海。

translations.literal: The army halted at Quanzhou, defeated Guoxuan, and drove him fleeing to sea.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Quanzhou it broke Liu Guoxuan's force and chased him back to sea.

sentences.zh: 拉哈達上其功，再予優敘，遷翰林學士。

translations.literal: Lahada reported his merits; he was again specially rewarded and transferred to Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Lahada submitted a report of his services, and Li Guangdi was again specially commended and promoted to Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 光地上疏推功將帥，辭新命，不允；

translations.literal: Guangdi submitted a memorial attributing the credit to the commanders and declining the new appointment; this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangdi memorialized, pushing the credit onto the generals and asking to be allowed to refuse the new rank, but the court would not accept his resignation.

sentences.zh: 並官日蠁，後積功官至永州總兵。

translations.literal: Ri Xiang was also given an official post, and later, through accumulated merit, rose to commander at Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ri Xiang was given an official appointment as well; by later accumulated service he rose to commander at Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 十九年，光地至京師，授內閣學士。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year Guangdi reached the capital and was appointed Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year Li Guangdi arrived in the capital and was made a Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 入對，言：「鄭錦已死，子克塽幼弱，部下爭權，宜急取之。」

translations.literal: On entering audience he said: "Zheng Jing is already dead; his son Keshuang is young and weak, and his subordinates are contending for power. We should seize the opportunity and take them quickly.
translations.idiomatic: In audience he said, "Zheng Jing is dead, his son Keshuang is still a child, and his officers are fighting among themselves. The court should move quickly to take them.

sentences.zh: 且舉內大臣施琅習海上形勢，知兵，可重任，上用其言，卒平台灣。

translations.literal: He also recommended Inner Minister Shi Lang, who knew the conditions at sea and understood warfare, as one who could be heavily entrusted; the emperor adopted his advice, and in the end Taiwan was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He also recommended the inner minister Shi Lang, who knew the seas and the art of war and could be trusted with a major command. The emperor took his counsel, and Taiwan was finally pacified.

sentences.zh: 陳夢雷者，侯官人。

translations.literal: Chen Menglei was a native of Houguan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Menglei came from Houguan.

sentences.zh: 與光地同歲舉進士，同官編修。

translations.literal: He and Guangdi passed the jinshi examination in the same year and held the same post as Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He and Li Guangdi had taken the jinshi in the same year and both served as Hanlin compilers.

sentences.zh: 方家居，精忠亂作，光地使日蠁潛詣夢雷探消息，得虛實，約並具疏密陳破賊狀，光地獨上之，由是大受寵眷。

translations.literal: While both were at home, Jingzhong's rebellion broke out; Guangdi sent Ri Xiang secretly to Menglei to gather intelligence, learned the true situation, and agreed that they would together draw up a memorial secretly reporting conditions for defeating the rebels; Guangdi alone submitted it, and from this he came to enjoy great imperial favor.
translations.idiomatic: While they were both living at home, Geng Jingzhong's rebellion erupted. Li Guangdi sent Ri Xiang in secret to Chen Menglei to learn what was really happening; once they knew the facts, they agreed to prepare a joint secret memorial on how the rebels might be broken. Li Guangdi submitted it alone, and from that moment he won extraordinary favor at court.

sentences.zh: 及精忠敗，夢雷以附逆逮京師，下獄論斬。

translations.literal: When Jingzhong was defeated, Menglei was arrested and sent to the capital for joining the rebellion, imprisoned, and sentenced to decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: After Geng Jingzhong fell, Chen Menglei was seized for having sided with the rebels, sent to the capital, imprisoned, and condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 光地乃疏陳兩次密約狀，夢雷得減死戍奉天。

translations.literal: Guangdi then submitted a memorial describing the two secret agreements, and Menglei had his sentence reduced from death to exile in Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangdi then memorialized, setting out the two secret agreements, and Chen Menglei's sentence was commuted from death to exile in Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，乞假奉母歸。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he requested leave to return home and serve his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he asked for leave to go home and care for his mother.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，還京，授翰林院掌院學士，直經筵，兼充日講起居注官，教習庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he returned to the capital, was appointed Chief Academician of the Hanlin Academy, attended the Classics Lectures, also served as Daily Lecturer and Recorder of Attendance and Departure, and instructed the junior Hanlin bachelors.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he came back to the capital, was made Chief Hanlin Academician, attended the emperor at the Classics Lectures, served concurrently as Daily Lecturer and Attendance Recorder, and tutored the junior Hanlin bachelors.

sentences.zh: 逾年，以母病乞歸省。

translations.literal: The following year, on account of his mother's illness, he requested leave to return and visit her.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when his mother fell ill, he asked to go home and see her.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，至京。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 初，光地與侍讀學士德格勒善，於上前互相稱引。

translations.literal: Earlier, Guangdi had been on good terms with Reader-in-Waiting Degele, and before the emperor each recommended the other.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Guangdi had been close to Reader-in-Waiting Degele, and the two had praised each other before the throne.

sentences.zh: 上召德格勒與諸詞臣試乾清宮，以文字劣，鐫秩。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Degele and the other literary officials to an examination in the Qianqing Palace; because his writing was inferior, his rank was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Degele and the other literary officials to a writing test in the Qianqing Palace; Degele's work was judged poor and his rank was lowered.

sentences.zh: 旋掌院庫勒訥劾其私抹起居注事，下獄論罪。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Chief Academician Kule'ne impeached him for privately altering the records of attendance and departure; he was imprisoned and sentenced.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Chief Academician Kule'ne impeached him for privately tampering with the attendance records, and he was jailed and convicted.

sentences.zh: 詔責光地，光地引罪，乞嚴譴，上原之。

translations.literal: An edict rebuked Guangdi; Guangdi acknowledged guilt and asked for severe punishment, and the emperor pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict censured Li Guangdi. He accepted blame and begged for stern punishment, but the emperor forgave him.

sentences.zh: 尋擢兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was promoted to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 三十年，典會試。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he presided over the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year he served as chief examiner for the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 偕侍郎博霽、徐廷璽，原任河督靳輔勘視河工。

translations.literal: Together with Vice Ministers Boji and Xu Tingxi, he joined former Director-General of Rivers Jin Fu in inspecting river works.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Vice Ministers Boji and Xu Tingxi, he accompanied the former Director-General of Rivers Jin Fu on an inspection of river engineering.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，督順天學政。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he was appointed Educational Commissioner of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year he was made Educational Commissioner of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 聞母喪，命在任守制。

translations.literal: When word came of his mother's death, he was ordered to remain in office while observing mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When news arrived of his mother's death, he was ordered to stay in his post and observe mourning there.

sentences.zh: 光地乞假九月回裡治喪。

translations.literal: Guangdi requested nine months' leave to return home and conduct the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangdi asked for nine months' leave to go home and bury his mother.

sentences.zh: 御史沈愷曾、楊敬儒交章論劾，上令遵初命。

translations.literal: Censors Shen Kaiyeng and Yang Jingru submitted successive memorials impeaching him, and the emperor ordered him to obey the original command.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Shen Kaiyeng and Yang Jingru filed memorial after memorial against him, and the emperor told him to follow the original order.

sentences.zh: 給事中彭鵬复疏論光地十不可留，目為貪位忘親，排詆尤力。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Peng Peng again submitted a memorial listing ten reasons Guangdi should not remain in office, calling him one who clung to rank and forgot his parent, and attacking him with especial force.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Peng Peng followed with a memorial setting out ten reasons Li Guangdi ought not remain in office, denouncing him as a man who coveted position and forgot his filial duty, and assailing him with unusual vehemence.

sentences.zh: 乃下九卿議，命光地解任，在京守制。

translations.literal: The court then referred the matter to the Nine Ministers for deliberation and ordered Guangdi relieved of his duties and to observe mourning in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The case was sent to the Nine Ministers for deliberation, and Li Guangdi was ordered to leave his post and mourn in the capital.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，服闋，仍督順天學政。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year, when his mourning ended, he again served as Educational Commissioner of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year, when his mourning was complete, he again became Educational Commissioner of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，授工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year he was appointed Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-sixth year he was appointed Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，出為直隸巡撫。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year he went out as Governor of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year he was sent out as Governor of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 初，畿輔屢遭水患，上以漳河與滹沱合流易汎濫，命光地導漳自故道引入運河，殺滹沱之勢。

translations.literal: Earlier the metropolitan region had repeatedly suffered from flooding; because the Zhang River and Hutuo River joined and easily overflowed, the emperor ordered Guangdi to divert the Zhang along its old course into the Grand Canal and reduce the force of the Hutuo.
translations.idiomatic: The capital region had long suffered floods. Because the Zhang and Hutuo rivers merged and easily burst their banks, the emperor ordered Li Guangdi to divert the Zhang along its old channel into the Grand Canal and weaken the Hutuo's force.

sentences.zh: 光地疏言：「漳河現分為三：一自廣平經魏、元城，至山東館陶入衛水歸運；

translations.literal: Guangdi submitted a memorial stating: "The Zhang River is now divided into three branches: one runs from Guangping through Wei and Yuancheng to Guantao in Shandong, enters the Wei River, and returns to the canal;
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangdi memorialized: "The Zhang River now divides into three branches. One runs from Guangping through Wei and Yuancheng to Guantao in Shandong, enters the Wei River, and rejoins the canal.

sentences.zh: 一為老漳河，自山東丘縣經南宮諸縣，與完固口合流，至鮑家嘴歸運；

translations.literal: one is the old Zhang River, which runs from Qiu County in Shandong through the counties of Nangong and others, joins the Wangu Pass stream, and at Baojia Mouth returns to the canal;
translations.idiomatic: One is the old Zhang River, which runs from Qiu County in Shandong through Nangong and the other counties, joins the stream at Wangu Pass, and at Baojia Mouth returns to the canal.

sentences.zh: 一為小漳河，自丘縣經廣宗、鉅鹿合於滏，又經束鹿、冀州合於滹沱。

translations.literal: one is the lesser Zhang River, which runs from Qiu County through Guangzong and Julu and joins the Fu River, then passes through Shulu and Jizhou and joins the Hutuo.
translations.idiomatic: One is the lesser Zhang River, which runs from Qiu County through Guangzong and Julu into the Fu River, then through Shulu and Jizhou into the Hutuo.

sentences.zh: 由衡水出獻縣完固口復分為兩支：小支與老漳河合流而歸運，大支經河間、大城、靜海入子牙河而歸淀。

translations.literal: From Hengshui it issues at Xian County's Wangu Pass and again divides into two branches: the lesser branch joins the old Zhang River and returns to the canal; the greater branch passes through Hejian, Dacheng, and Jinghai, enters the Ziya River, and returns to Lake Dian.
translations.idiomatic: From Hengshui it flows out at Wangu Pass in Xian County and splits again into two branches: the smaller branch merges with the old Zhang River and rejoins the canal; the larger branch runs through Hejian, Dacheng, and Jinghai, enters the Ziya River, and drains into Lake Dian.

sentences.zh: 今入衛之河與老漳河流淺而弱，宜疏濬；

translations.literal: At present the river entering the Wei and the old Zhang River run shallow and weak; they should be dredged;
translations.idiomatic: At present the branch entering the Wei and the old Zhang River are shallow and weak and should be dredged.

sentences.zh: 其完固口小支應築壩逼水入河，更於靜海閻、留二莊挑土築堤，束水歸淀，俾無汎濫。」

translations.literal: the lesser branch at Wangu Pass should be dammed to force the water into the canal, and at Yan and Liu villages in Jinghai earth should be excavated to build dikes, confining the water to Lake Dian so that it will not overflow.
translations.idiomatic: The lesser branch at Wangu Pass should be dammed to drive the water into the canal, and at the Yan and Liu villages in Jinghai earthworks should be raised to build dikes, channeling the water into Lake Dian and preventing floods.

sentences.zh: 詔報可。

translations.literal: An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the plan.

sentences.zh: 尋奏霸州、永清、宛平、良鄉、固安、高陽、獻縣因濬新河，佔民田一百三十九頃，請豁免賦額，從之。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he memorialized that in Bazhou, Yongqing, Wanping, Liangxiang, Gu'an, Gaoyang, and Xian County, because new rivers were dredged, one hundred thirty-nine qing of private fields were occupied, and he requested exemption from the tax quota; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He soon reported that dredging the new channels in Bazhou, Yongqing, Wanping, Liangxiang, Gu'an, Gaoyang, and Xian County had taken one hundred thirty-nine qing of private farmland, and asked that the tax on that land be remitted; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 通州等六州縣額設紅剝船六百號，剝運南漕，每船給贍田，遇水旱例不蠲免，光地奏請援民田例概蠲免之。

translations.literal: In the six prefectures and counties of Tongzhou and elsewhere six hundred red lighter-boats were established by quota to transship southern tribute grain; each boat was granted supporting fields, which in cases of flood or drought were by precedent not remitted, and Guangdi memorialized asking that the precedent for private fields be applied and all such taxes remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Tongzhou and five other prefectures and counties maintained six hundred official red lighter-boats for transshipping southern tribute grain; each boat was allotted supporting farmland whose taxes were not normally remitted in flood or drought years. Li Guangdi asked that the same remission granted private fields be applied to these allotments as well.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，上臨視子牙河工，命光地於獻縣東西兩岸築長堤，西接大城，東接靜海，亙二百餘裡；

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year the emperor personally inspected the Ziya River works and ordered Guangdi to build long dikes on the east and west banks at Xian County, extending west to Dacheng and east to Jinghai, more than two hundred li in all;
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year the emperor inspected the Ziya River works in person and ordered Li Guangdi to build long dikes on both banks at Xian County, running west to Dacheng and east to Jinghai, more than two hundred li in all.

sentences.zh: 又於靜海廣福樓、焦家口開新河，引水入淀：由是下流益暢，無水患。

translations.literal: he also opened new channels at Guangfu Tower and Jiaojiakou in Jinghai to lead water into Lake Dian; from this the lower reaches flowed more freely and there were no flood disasters.
translations.idiomatic: He also cut new channels at Guangfu Tower and Jiaojiakou in Jinghai to draw water into Lake Dian, after which the lower course ran more freely and the region was free of flooding.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，上褒其治績，擢吏部尚書，仍管巡撫事。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year the emperor praised his administrative achievements, promoted him to Minister of Personnel, and still left him in charge of the governorship.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year the emperor commended his record in office, promoted him to Minister of Personnel, and left him in charge of the governorship as before.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，給事中黃鼎楫、湯右曾、許志進、宋駿業、王原等合疏劾光地撫綏無狀，致河間饑民流入京畿，並寧津縣匿災不報狀。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year Supervising Secretaries Huang Dingji, Tang Youzeng, Xu Zhijin, Song Junye, Wang Yuan, and others jointly memorialized impeaching Guangdi for poor pacification and relief, causing famine refugees from Hejian to pour into the capital region, and also for concealing disaster reports in Ningjin County.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year Supervising Secretaries Huang Dingji, Tang Youzeng, Xu Zhijin, Song Junye, Wang Yuan, and others jointly impeached Li Guangdi for failing to govern and relieve the people properly, allowing famine refugees from Hejian to flood into the capital region, and for concealing disaster reports in Ningjin County.

sentences.zh: 光地疏辨，引咎乞罷，詔原之。

translations.literal: Guangdi submitted a memorial in rebuttal, acknowledged guilt, and asked to be dismissed; an edict pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangdi answered with a memorial of defense, accepted blame, and asked to be removed from office; the emperor pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 再疏辭尚書，不許。

translations.literal: He again memorialized to resign the ministership, but this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized again to resign the ministry, but was not allowed to do so.

sentences.zh: 尋疏劾雲南布政使張霖假稱詔旨，販鬻私鹽，得銀百六十餘萬，霖論斬，籍沒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he memorialized impeaching Zhang Lin, Financial Commissioner of Yunnan, for falsely claiming an imperial edict and privately selling salt, obtaining more than 1,600,000 taels of silver; Lin was sentenced to decapitation and his property was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: He soon impeached Zhang Lin, Financial Commissioner of Yunnan, for falsely invoking an imperial edict while trafficking in private salt and amassing more than 1,600,000 taels of silver. Zhang Lin was sentenced to death and his property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，拜文淵閣大學士。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fourth year he was made Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 時上潛心理學，旁闡六藝，御纂硃子全書及周易折中、性理精義諸書，皆命光地校理，日召入便殿揅求探討。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor devoted himself secretly to Neo-Confucian learning, broadly expounded the Six Arts, and personally compiled the Complete Works of Zhu Xi, the Balanced Commentaries on the Book of Changes, and Essentials of Principle and Nature, among other books; all were ordered to be collated by Guangdi, who was daily summoned into the privy chamber to refine and discuss them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then immersed in Neo-Confucian learning, extending his studies into the Six Arts. The imperial compilations—the Complete Works of Zhu Xi, the Balanced Commentaries on the Book of Changes, the Essentials of Principle and Nature, and other such works—were all entrusted to Li Guangdi for collation, and he was summoned daily into the privy chamber to refine and discuss them.

sentences.zh: 四十七年，皇太子允礽以疾廢，命諸大臣保奏諸皇子孰可當儲位者。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year the heir apparent Yinreng was deposed on account of illness, and the emperor ordered the great ministers to recommend which of the princes should be appointed heir.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-seventh year the crown prince Yinreng was set aside because of illness, and the emperor ordered the senior ministers to recommend which prince ought to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 尚書王鴻緒等舉皇子允禩，上切責之。

translations.literal: Minister Wang Hongxu and others recommended Prince YinSi, and the emperor sharply rebuked them.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Wang Hongxu and others recommended Prince YinSi, and the emperor rebuked them sharply.

sentences.zh: 詢光地何無一言，光地奏：「前者皇上問臣以廢太子病，臣奏言徐徐調治，天下之福，臣未嘗告諸人也。」

translations.literal: He asked why Guangdi had not spoken; Guangdi replied: "Earlier, when Your Majesty asked me about the deposed crown prince's illness, I answered that he should be slowly nursed back to health, which would be a blessing for the realm. I have never told this to anyone else.
translations.idiomatic: He asked why Li Guangdi had said nothing. Li Guangdi answered, "When Your Majesty earlier asked me about the deposed crown prince's illness, I said he should be nursed back to health by degrees, which would be the realm's good fortune. I have never told that to anyone else.

sentences.zh: 光地被上遇，同列多忌之者，凡所稱薦，多見排擠，因以撼光地。

translations.literal: Guangdi enjoyed the emperor's favor; many of his colleagues envied him, and those he recommended were often obstructed, and in this way attacks were made against Guangdi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangdi enjoyed exceptional favor with the emperor, and many colleagues envied him. Those he recommended were often blocked, and his enemies used that to undermine him.

sentences.zh: 撫直隸時，御史呂履恆劾光地於秋審事任意斷決，上察其不實，還其奏。

translations.literal: While governing Zhili, Censor Lü Lüheng impeached Guangdi for arbitrary decisions in autumn review cases; the emperor found this untrue and returned the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: While he was governor of Zhili, Censor Lü Lüheng accused Li Guangdi of deciding autumn review cases arbitrarily; the emperor saw that the charge was false and sent the memorial back.

sentences.zh: 給事中王原劾文選郎中陳汝弼受贓，法司論絞，汝弼，光地所薦也。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Wang Yuan impeached Chen Rubi, Director in the Bureau of Appointments, for taking bribes; the judicial offices sentenced him to strangulation; Rubi had been recommended by Guangdi.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Wang Yuan accused Chen Rubi, a director in the Bureau of Appointments, of taking bribes. The judicial offices sentenced him to death by strangulation. Chen Rubi had been Li Guangdi's nominee.

sentences.zh: 上察其供證非實，下廷臣確核，得逼供行賄狀，汝弼免罪，承讞官降革有差，原奪官。

translations.literal: The emperor found that the testimony was not true, ordered the court ministers to verify the facts, discovered that confessions had been forced and bribes fabricated; Rubi was cleared of guilt, the officials who had framed the case were demoted or dismissed in varying degrees, and Wang Yuan was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged the evidence false and ordered a thorough review by the court. Forced confessions and fabricated bribery came to light. Chen Rubi was cleared, the officials who had framed him were demoted or dismissed in varying degrees, and Wang Yuan lost his post.

sentences.zh: 光地益敬慎，其有獻納，罕見於章奏。

translations.literal: Guangdi became all the more reverent and cautious; his remonstrances and recommendations rarely appeared in formal memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangdi grew still more cautious and restrained; the advice he offered seldom appeared in formal memorials.

sentences.zh: 江寧知府陳鵬年忤總督阿山，坐事論重闢，光地言其誣，鵬年遂內召。

translations.literal: Chen Pengnian, Prefect of Jiangning, offended Governor Ashan, was convicted and sentenced to heavy punishment; Guangdi said the charge was false, and Pengnian was then summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Pengnian, prefect of Jiangning, offended Governor Ashan, was convicted on a charge that carried severe punishment. Li Guangdi declared the case a frame-up, and Chen Pengnian was summoned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 兩江總督噶禮與巡撫張伯行互訐，遣大臣往訊，久不決。

translations.literal: Governor-General Gali and Governor Zhang Boxing impeached each other; grand ministers were dispatched to investigate, and for a long time no decision was reached.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Gali and Governor Zhang Boxing denounced each other. Grand ministers were sent to investigate, but the case dragged on without resolution.

sentences.zh: 嗣詔罷噶禮，复伯行官，光地實讚之。

translations.literal: Later an edict dismissed Gali and restored Boxing to office; Guangdi had in fact supported this.
translations.idiomatic: An edict eventually removed Gali and restored Zhang Boxing to office—a outcome Li Guangdi had quietly favored.

sentences.zh: 桐城貢士方苞坐戴名世獄論死，上偶言及侍郎汪霦卒後，誰能作古文者，光地曰：「惟戴名世案內方苞能。」

translations.literal: Fang Bao of Tongcheng, a presented scholar, was sentenced to death in the Dai Mingshi case; the emperor happened to mention that after Vice Minister Wang Lin's death, who could write ancient-style prose, and Guangdi said: "Only Fang Bao, within the Dai Mingshi case, is capable.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Bao of Tongcheng, a presented scholar, had been condemned to death in the Dai Mingshi case. When the emperor casually asked, after Vice Minister Wang Lin's death, who could write ancient-style prose, Li Guangdi said, "Only Fang Bao, the man implicated in the Dai Mingshi case, has that ability.

sentences.zh: 苞得釋，召入南書房。

translations.literal: Bao was released and summoned into the Southern Studio.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Bao was released and called into the Southern Studio.

sentences.zh: 其扶植善類如此。

translations.literal: In supporting worthy men he was like this.
translations.idiomatic: This was the way he lifted up men of talent.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，與千叟宴，賜賚有加。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year he attended the banquet for a thousand elders and received especially generous gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-second year he attended the banquet for elders of a thousand years and received especially generous gifts.

sentences.zh: 頃之，以病乞休，溫旨慰留。

translations.literal: Before long, on account of illness he requested retirement; a warm edict comforted him and asked him to remain.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he asked to retire on grounds of illness; a warm edict comforted him and urged him to stay.

sentences.zh: 越二年，復以為請，且言母喪未葬，許給假二年，賜詩寵行。

translations.literal: Two years later he again made the request, and also said his mother's funeral had not yet been conducted; he was granted two years' leave and received an imperial poem honoring his departure.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he asked again, adding that his mother's burial was still unfinished. He was granted two years' leave and sent off with an imperial poem.

sentences.zh: 五十六年，還朝，累疏乞罷，上以大學士王掞方在告，暫止之。

translations.literal: In the fifty-sixth year he returned to court, repeatedly memorialized asking to be dismissed, and the emperor temporarily stopped this because Grand Secretary Wang Yan was already on leave.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-sixth year he returned to court and repeatedly asked to be dismissed, but the emperor held off because Grand Secretary Wang Yan was already away on leave.

sentences.zh: 五十七年，卒，年七十七，遣恆親王允祺奠醊，賜金千兩，諡文貞。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year he died at the age of seventy-seven; Prince Heng Yinqi was sent to offer libations, one thousand taels of silver were granted, and he was posthumously given the honorific Wen Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-seventh year he died at seventy-seven. Prince Heng Yinqi was sent to offer libations, one thousand taels of silver were granted, and he was posthumously honored as Wen Zhen.

sentences.zh: 使工部尚書徐元夢護其喪歸，复諭閣臣：「李光地謹慎清勤，始終一節，學問淵博。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Xu Yuanmeng was sent to escort the funeral home, and the emperor again instructed the grand secretaries: "Li Guangdi was careful, pure, and diligent, consistent from beginning to end, and his learning was broad and deep.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Xu Yuanmeng was sent to escort the bier home, and the emperor again told the grand secretaries, "Li Guangdi was careful, pure, and diligent, unwavering to the end, and his learning was broad and deep.

sentences.zh: 朕知之最真，知朕亦無過光地者！」

translations.literal: I know this most truly, and among those who know me none surpasses Guangdi!
translations.idiomatic: I know this better than anyone, and among those who truly know me, none surpasses Li Guangdi!

sentences.zh: 雍正初，贈太子太傅，祀賢良祠。

translations.literal: In the early Yongzheng reign he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and enshrined in the Shrine of Worthy Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongzheng reign he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and entered the Shrine of Worthy Ministers.

sentences.zh: 弟光坡，性至孝，家居不仕，潛心經術。

translations.literal: His younger brother Guangpo was utterly filial by nature, lived at home and did not take office, and devoted himself to the classics.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Guangpo was profoundly filial by nature. He lived at home without taking office and devoted himself to classical learning.

sentences.zh: 子鍾倫，舉人，治經史性理，旁及諸子百家，從其叔父光坡治三禮，於周官、禮記尤精，稱其家學。

translations.literal: His son Zhonglun, a provincial graduate, studied the classics, histories, and Neo-Confucian principle and nature, and also the various masters and the hundred schools; he followed his uncle Guangpo in studying the Three Rites and was especially expert in the Offices of Zhou and the Book of Rites, which their family learning was praised for.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhonglun, a provincial graduate, studied the classics, histories, and Neo-Confucian moral philosophy, as well as the masters and the hundred schools. He studied the Three Rites under his uncle Guangpo and was especially accomplished in the Offices of Zhou and the Book of Rites; their household learning was widely admired.

sentences.zh: 從子天寵，進士，官編修，有志操，邃於經學，與弟鍾僑、鍾旺俱以窮經講學為業。

translations.literal: His nephew Tianchong, a jinshi, served as Compiler; he had integrity and purpose and was deeply versed in classical learning; with his brothers Zhongqiao and Zhongwang he all made the exhaustive study and teaching of the classics their profession.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Tianchong, a jinshi and Hanlin compiler, had strong moral purpose and deep learning in the classics. He and his brothers Zhongqiao and Zhongwang all devoted themselves to rigorous classical study and teaching.

sentences.zh: 鍾僑進士，官編修，督學江西，以實行課士，左遷國子監丞。

translations.literal: Zhongqiao, a jinshi and Compiler, served as Educational Commissioner of Jiangxi; because he tested scholars on practical conduct he was demoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongqiao, a jinshi and compiler, served as Educational Commissioner of Jiangxi. Because he judged candidates by real conduct rather than form alone, he was demoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 鍾旺，舉人，授中書，充性理精義纂修官。

translations.literal: Zhongwang, a provincial graduate, was appointed Secretary in the Grand Secretariat and served as a compiler for the Essentials of Principle and Nature.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwang, a provincial graduate, was appointed a secretarial officer in the Grand Secretariat and served on the editorial staff of the Essentials of Principle and Nature.

sentences.zh: 論曰：聖祖崇儒重道，經筵講論，孜孜聖賢之學，朝臣承其化，一時成為風氣。

translations.literal: The historians comment: The Sacred Ancestor honored Confucian learning and valued the Way; at the Classics Lectures he discussed the learning of the sages with tireless zeal, and the court ministers received his transforming influence until it became the temper of the age.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: Emperor Kangxi honored Confucian learning and held the Way in esteem. At the Classics Lectures he pursued the teachings of the sages with tireless zeal, and the ministers of the court were shaped by that influence until it became the temper of the age.

sentences.zh: 裔介久官臺諫，數進讜言，為憂盛危明之計，自登政府，柴立不阿，奉身早退，有古大臣之風。

translations.literal: Yijie long served in the censorate, repeatedly offered forthright counsel, and planned for the age when prosperity hides danger; once he entered the government he stood upright like firewood and would not bend, retired early from office, and had the bearing of the great ministers of old.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yijie spent years in the censorate, offering forthright counsel again and again and thinking in terms of guarding against danger in times of prosperity. Once in the central government he stood straight as stacked firewood and would not yield, retired early, and carried himself like the great ministers of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 賜履剛方鯁直，疏舉經筵，冀裨主德，庶乎以道事君者歟？

translations.literal: Cilv was stern, upright, and blunt; he memorialized urging the Classics Lectures, hoping to aid the emperor's virtue—perhaps one who served his ruler by the Way?
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Cilv was stern, upright, and blunt. He memorialized in favor of the Classics Lectures, hoping to strengthen the emperor's virtue—perhaps a man who truly served his ruler through the Way.

sentences.zh: 光地易攵歷中外，得君最專，而疑叢業集，委蛇進退，務為韜默。

translations.literal: Guangdi served in posts at court and in the provinces, enjoyed the emperor's favor more exclusively than others, yet suspicions clustered thickly around him; in advance and retreat he was supple and accommodating, striving to remain taciturn.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangdi served both at court and in the provinces and enjoyed the emperor's trust more fully than anyone, yet suspicion gathered around him in thickets. He moved through office with supple caution, doing his best to keep silent.

sentences.zh: 聖祖嘗論道學不在空言，先行後言，君子所尚。

translations.literal: The Sacred Ancestor once remarked that Neo-Confucian learning does not lie in empty words; action comes first and words after, and this is what the gentleman honors.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Kangxi once said that Neo-Confucian learning is not a matter of empty talk: deed must come before word, and that is what the gentleman values.

sentences.zh: 夫道學豈易言哉？

translations.literal: Can the learning of the Way be spoken of easily?
translations.idiomatic: But is the learning of the Way so easily spoken of?
